# Aipim: complete documentation for language models

Everything an agent needs in one file: the rules (AGENTS.md), the foundations and the spec of every component. Generated by tools/build_ai.py: do not edit by hand.

---

# AGENTS.md: building with Aipim

<!-- description:start -->
Aipim is a small, open, Brazilian design system with all the parts in place: foundations (tokens), 24 HTML and CSS components, 64 line icons, one Markdown spec per component and a token generator that enforces accessibility checks. Made to be customized, and to be used by people and by AI agents.
<!-- description:end -->
This file tells an AI agent how to build interfaces with it. Read it first, then read the spec of every component you use.

- Repository: https://github.com/talis-galhardi/aipim
- Index for agents: `llms.txt` (links) and `llms-full.txt` (everything in one file)
- Specs: `docs/en/components/<name>.md`. Step-by-step tutorials for designers, developers and AI agents: `docs/en/tutorials-designers.md`, `docs/en/tutorials-developers.md` and `docs/en/tutorials-ai.md`. Words in the interface: `docs/en/voice-and-microcopy.md`. What was verified: `docs/en/verification.md`. Brand patterns and the ornament: `docs/en/patterns-and-ornament.md`. Foundations: `docs/en/color.md`, `docs/en/typography.md`, `docs/en/space-shape-motion.md`. The same docs in Brazilian Portuguese are in `docs/pt-br/`, with the same file names

## The rules

1. **Colors come from semantic tokens only.** Use `var(--aipim-bg-surface)`, `var(--aipim-text-primary)`, `var(--aipim-action-primary-bg)` and the other roles in `docs/en/color.md`. Never write a hex value. Never use a primitive (`--aipim-color-primary-700`) inside a component: primitives exist to generate the roles and to customize.
2. **Spacing, radius, borders, sizes, durations and z-index come from tokens.** `var(--aipim-space-16)`, `var(--aipim-radius-md)`, `var(--aipim-border-thin)`, `var(--aipim-size-control-md)`, `var(--aipim-duration-base)`. If a value has no token, the spec of that component says so.
3. **State is never shown by color alone.** Every state carries an icon and text (an error has an icon and a message, a selected tab has a bar).
4. **Use native elements.** `button` for actions, `a` for navigation, `input` with a real `label`, `dialog` for modals, `nav` and `header` for landmarks.
5. **Every interactive element has a visible focus ring**: `outline: var(--aipim-border-thick) solid var(--aipim-focus-ring); outline-offset: var(--aipim-focus-offset)` on `:focus-visible`. The components already do this. Do not remove it.
6. **A button with only an icon needs an `aria-label`.** The icon itself is `aria-hidden="true"`. Use the Icon button component for that.
7. **Disabled** means the native `disabled` attribute (or `aria-disabled="true"` on a link). The look comes from `--aipim-opacity-disabled`.
8. **Headings use Antonio, text uses Karla**, through the text tokens (`--aipim-text-h2-size`, `--aipim-text-body-size` and so on). Body text is at least 16px.
9. **Dark theme is an attribute**: `<html data-theme="dark">`, or it follows the system. Never hard-code a color for one theme.
10. **No `!important`.** To customize a component, set its own variables (`--aipim-button-bg`, `--aipim-button-height` and the others in its CSS) or override the semantic tokens.
11. **Do not edit generated files**: `tokens/build/*`, `tokens/tokens.json`, `docs/{en,pt-br}/color.md`, `docs/{en,pt-br}/typography.md`, `docs/{en,pt-br}/space-shape-motion.md`, the tutorials in `docs/{en,pt-br}/`, `components/web/aipim-components.css`, `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt`, and the parts between markers: the light and dark colors of the specs' token tables (`tools/build_specs.py`), the masks and the checks of the Brazilian field inside `components/web/aipim.js` (from `components/web/aipim-br.js`, `tools/build_web.py`), the icons inline in the gallery and the theme builder (`tools/build_web.py`), the component lists in this file, `.storybook/i18n.js` and `stories/_gallery.js`, and the description at the top of this file (`tools/build_ai.py`, from `package.json`). Change the source and rebuild (see "Verify").
12. **Text follows the voice**: warm, direct, specific. An error says what happened and what to do, without blaming ("Check your card details and try again", not "Something went wrong"). Buttons use verbs.

## Set up

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Antonio:wght@600;700&family=Karla:wght@400;700&display=swap">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="tokens/build/css/aipim.css">      <!-- tokens (--aipim-*), light and dark -->
<link rel="stylesheet" href="components/web/aipim-components.css"> <!-- all components; or load only the files you need -->
<script src="components/web/aipim.js"></script>                 <!-- optional: tabs keys, dismiss buttons, dialog commands -->

<body style="background:var(--aipim-bg-canvas);color:var(--aipim-text-primary);font:var(--aipim-text-body-size) var(--aipim-font-body)">
```

Icons: `<svg class="aipim-icon" aria-hidden="true"><use href="icons/sprite.svg#aipim-close"></use></svg>`. The 64 names are in `icons/icons.json`.

## Components

Class names are `aipim-<component>`, parts are `aipim-<component>__<part>`, variants are `aipim-<component>--<variant>`.

<!-- components:start -->
| Component | Root class | Use it for | Spec |
|---|---|---|---|
| Avatar | `aipim-avatar` | A person or a thing inside a circle: a photo, the initials on a tone, or an icon. | `docs/en/components/avatar.md` |
| Badge | `aipim-badge` | A small mark with a numeral or an icon, next to text. Decorative. | `docs/en/components/badge.md` |
| Button | `aipim-button` | The main action of a screen or block. | `docs/en/components/button.md` |
| Checkbox | `aipim-checkbox` | Lets a person pick any number of independent options. | `docs/en/components/checkbox.md` |
| Icon button | `aipim-icon-button` | A button that shows only an icon. | `docs/en/components/icon-button.md` |
| Link | `aipim-link` | Takes the reader to another page or section. | `docs/en/components/link.md` |
| Radio | `aipim-radio` | Lets a person pick one option from a short list. | `docs/en/components/radio.md` |
| Switch | `aipim-switch` | Turns a setting on or off, and the change applies right away. | `docs/en/components/switch.md` |
| Tag | `aipim-tag` | A short label for a category, a technology or a status. | `docs/en/components/tag.md` |
| Accordion | `aipim-accordion` | A title that opens a panel of text, to hide what most people do not need to read. | `docs/en/components/accordion.md` |
| Alert | `aipim-alert` | An important message that stays visible on the page. | `docs/en/components/alert.md` |
| Brazilian field | `aipim-field` | A text field for Brazilian data (CPF, CNPJ, CEP, phone, date and reais), with its mask and its check. | `docs/en/components/brazilian-field.md` |
| Card | `aipim-card` | Groups related content on one surface. It can be a single link. | `docs/en/components/card.md` |
| Combobox | `aipim-combobox` | A text field that filters a list of options while you type, for long lists such as the states of Brazil or the banks. | `docs/en/components/combobox.md` |
| Datepicker | `aipim-datepicker` | A Brazilian date field with a button that opens a calendar, for dates near today such as a delivery or an appointment. | `docs/en/components/datepicker.md` |
| Empty state | `aipim-empty-state` | What a list, search or area shows when there is nothing to show yet. | `docs/en/components/empty-state.md` |
| List item | `aipim-list-item` | One row of a list, with a start, a title and a description, and an end that is a chevron, a value or a switch. | `docs/en/components/list-item.md` |
| Select | `aipim-select` | Lets a person pick one option from a list that opens, when the options do not fit on screen as radio buttons. | `docs/en/components/select.md` |
| Tabs | `aipim-tabs` | Switches between views of the same content. | `docs/en/components/tabs.md` |
| Text field | `aipim-field` | A single-line field for short typed text, with a visible label above it. | `docs/en/components/text-field.md` |
| Toast | `aipim-toast` | A quick confirmation that goes away on its own. | `docs/en/components/toast.md` |
| Modal | `aipim-modal` | A decision or short task that needs attention, on top of the page. | `docs/en/components/modal.md` |
| Tab bar | `aipim-tab-bar` | The main navigation on phones, with three to five destinations. | `docs/en/components/tab-bar.md` |
| Top bar | `aipim-top-bar` | The title of a screen, with a back button and up to two actions. | `docs/en/components/top-bar.md` |
<!-- components:end -->

## Patterns that are easy to get wrong

- **A form field has its label above it**, always visible; the placeholder never replaces it. Helper and error text are linked with `aria-describedby`, and an invalid field has `aria-invalid="true"`.
- **A badge is decorative**: it has `aria-hidden="true"` and the meaning stays in the text next to it. Never use one alone to show information.
- **One primary button per screen.** The other actions are secondary, outline or ghost.
- **Errors that stay on the page are an Alert** (`role="alert"` for errors, `role="status"` for the rest). A passing confirmation is a Toast. A decision that needs attention is a Modal.
- **A clickable card is one link**: the link is inside the title and covers the card. Do not put buttons or links inside an interactive card.
- **Tabs switch views of the same content; the Tab bar moves between the main sections of an app.** Do not use one for the other.
- **A modal is a `dialog` opened with `showModal()`** (or `command="show-modal"`), with a title linked by `aria-labelledby` and a close button.
- **Do not nest components that compete** (a card in a card, two primary buttons side by side).

## Verify

```bash
python3 tools/check.py      # every quick check (or npm run check): contrast, the generated files, the numbers in the docs, the breakpoints, copy, translation
npm run check:browser       # in a browser: the components (axe, keyboard, zoom, reflow), the theme builder and the Storybook (needs Playwright and npm install)
```

A check that finds a generated file out of date names the script that rebuilds it.

Open `components/web/examples/index.html` to see every component with a light and dark toggle.

Before you finish a screen, check:

- [ ] Only `--aipim-*` variables for color and size, no hex
- [ ] A media query breaks at 600, 1024 or 1440 (the breakpoint scale), written as a range: `@media (width < 600px)`
- [ ] Every control reachable and visible by keyboard
- [ ] Every icon-only button has an `aria-label`
- [ ] Every field has a visible label
- [ ] No state conveyed by color alone
- [ ] It works in light and dark, and at 200% zoom

## Customize

The palette is generated. Without code, use the theme builder (`theme-builder/`, online at https://talisgalhardi.com/aipim/theme-builder/): it exports a CSS file to load after `aipim.css` and a theme for the Figma plugin (`figma-plugin/`). In code, open `tools/build_tokens.py`, change the seeds at the top (hue and chroma per color) and run `python3 tools/build_tokens.py`. It rebuilds every scale and output and fails if a pair no longer meets contrast.

# Colors

Generated from `tokens/tokens.json`. Use **only the semantic roles** in components; primitives exist to generate the roles and to customize. To use your brand colors without code, make a theme in the [theme builder](https://talisgalhardi.com/aipim/theme-builder/?lang=en).

## Ramps (primitives)

| Ramp | Origin | Steps |
|---|---|---|
| `primary` | Urucum: annatto red-orange | 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800, 900 |
| `secondary` | Azulejo: a clear, saturated blue (also the link color) | 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800, 900 |
| `tertiary` | Cajá: sunny yellow | 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800, 900 |
| `success` | Leaf: bright green | 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800, 900 |
| `error` | Cherry red, away from the primary | 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800, 900 |
| `neutral` | Almost-gray brown, tinted with earth | 50, 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800, 900, 950, 1000 |

## Accessibility (WCAG 2.2)

88 of 88 checks pass, in both modes. Body text at AAA (7:1), supporting text at AA (4.5:1), components and icons at 3:1.

|---|---|---|---|

| Dark | Info, icon (3:1): `info.icon` on `info.bg` | 6.41:1 | 3 |
| Dark | Text on primary tint (AAA): `tint.text` on `tint.primary` | 8.66:1 | 7 |
| Dark | Text on secondary tint (AAA): `tint.text` on `tint.secondary` | 8.21:1 | 7 |
| Dark | Text on tertiary tint (AAA): `tint.text` on `tint.tertiary` | 8.08:1 | 7 |
| Dark | Text on success tint (AAA): `tint.text` on `tint.success` | 7.67:1 | 7 |
| Dark | Text on error tint (AAA): `tint.text` on `tint.error` | 8.82:1 | 7 |
| Dark | Supporting text on primary tint (AA): `tint.text.muted` on `tint.primary` | 7.27:1 | 4.5 |
| Dark | Supporting text on secondary tint (AA): `tint.text.muted` on `tint.secondary` | 6.90:1 | 4.5 |
| Dark | Supporting text on tertiary tint (AA): `tint.text.muted` on `tint.tertiary` | 6.78:1 | 4.5 |
| Dark | Supporting text on success tint (AA): `tint.text.muted` on `tint.success` | 6.44:1 | 4.5 |
| Dark | Supporting text on error tint (AA): `tint.text.muted` on `tint.error` | 7.40:1 | 4.5 |

## Rules

- Never convey state by color alone: always icon and text.
- Accent color is not a running-text color.
- Placeholder uses `text.muted`.
- Focus ring of 3px with a 3px offset.


---

# Typography

Generated from `tokens/tokens.json`. Headings in **Antonio** (uppercase), body in **Karla**. Everything in `rem`, fluid between 360px and 1280px.

| Style | Family | Mobile → desktop | Line-height | Weight | Tracking |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `display` | Antonio, uppercase | 48 → 72px | 1.1 | 700 | 0.01em |
| `h1` | Antonio, uppercase | 40 → 56px | 1.1 | 700 | 0.01em |
| `h2` | Antonio, uppercase | 32 → 44px | 1.1 | 700 | 0.01em |
| `h3` | Antonio, uppercase | 28 → 32px | 1.15 | 700 | 0.01em |
| `h4` | Antonio, uppercase | 22 → 24px | 1.2 | 600 | 0.02em |
| `body-lg` | Karla | 18 → 18px | 1.6 | 400 | 0em |
| `body` | Karla | 16 → 16px | 1.5 | 400 | 0em |
| `body-sm` | Karla | 14 → 14px | 1.5 | 400 | 0em |
| `label` | Karla | 16 → 16px | 1.25 | 700 | 0.01em |
| `overline` | Karla, uppercase | 12 → 12px | 1.5 | 700 | 0.08em |

## Rules

- Body `line-height` of at least 1.5; headings at least 1.1 (accents on capitals).
- Columns at most 70 characters wide.
- Nothing essential at 12px (`overline` is only for non-essential information).
- The layout must not break with increased text spacing (WCAG 1.4.12).


---

# Space, shape and motion

Generated from `tokens/tokens.json`. Spacing is a base-4 scale. Use the **role** tokens (`inset`, `stack`, `gap`) when the meaning is clear and the raw scale when it is not.

## Spacing scale

| Token | CSS variable | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `space/0` | `--aipim-space-0` | 0px | No space |
| `space/4` | `--aipim-space-4` | 4px | Tight gaps: icon to text inside a tag, destinations in a bar |
| `space/8` | `--aipim-space-8` | 8px | Gap between an icon and its label, between small items |
| `space/12` | `--aipim-space-12` | 12px | Gap between text parts, between buttons in a group |
| `space/16` | `--aipim-space-16` | 16px | Default padding and gap between related blocks |
| `space/24` | `--aipim-space-24` | 24px | Padding of a card, gap between cards |
| `space/32` | `--aipim-space-32` | 32px | Padding of a dialog or an empty state |
| `space/48` | `--aipim-space-48` | 48px | Padding of large panels, gap between large blocks |
| `space/64` | `--aipim-space-64` | 64px | Space around a section |
| `space/80` | `--aipim-space-80` | 80px | Large vertical rhythm |
| `space/96` | `--aipim-space-96` | 96px | Largest space, between page areas |

## Spacing roles

| Token | CSS variable | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `space-role/stack.tight` | `--aipim-stack-tight` | 8px |
| `space-role/stack.normal` | `--aipim-stack-normal` | 16px |
| `space-role/stack.loose` | `--aipim-stack-loose` | 24px |
| `space-role/inset.sm` | `--aipim-inset-sm` | 12px |
| `space-role/inset.md` | `--aipim-inset-md` | 16px |
| `space-role/inset.lg` | `--aipim-inset-lg` | 24px |
| `space-role/inset.xl` | `--aipim-inset-xl` | 32px |
| `space-role/gap.grid` | `--aipim-gap-grid` | 24px |

Inset is the padding inside a component, stack is the vertical gap between siblings, gap is the gap in a grid.

## Corner radius

| Token | CSS variable | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `radius/none` | `--aipim-radius-none` | 0px | Square corners |
| `radius/sm` | `--aipim-radius-sm` | 4px | Checkbox, tab, small icon button |
| `radius/md` | `--aipim-radius-md` | 8px | Buttons, fields, alerts, icon buttons |
| `radius/lg` | `--aipim-radius-lg` | 12px | Toasts and illustration slots |
| `radius/xl` | `--aipim-radius-xl` | 16px | Cards |
| `radius/2xl` | `--aipim-radius-2xl` | 24px | Dialog panels |
| `radius/full` | `--aipim-radius-full` | 999px | Tags and switches: fully round |

## Border and focus

| Token | CSS variable | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `border/thin` | `--aipim-border-thin` | 1px | Dividers and card borders |
| `border/medium` | `--aipim-border-medium` | 2px | Field and button borders |
| `border/thick` | `--aipim-border-thick` | 3px | Focus ring width and selected bars |
| `focus/offset` | `--aipim-focus-offset` | 3px | Gap between an element and its focus ring |

Width and color are separate decisions: the width comes from `border/*` and the color from `border/subtle` or `border/strong`.

## Sizes

| Token | CSS variable | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `size/touch.min` | `--aipim-size-touch-min` | 24px | Smallest target that meets WCAG 2.5.8 (24px) |
| `size/touch.comfortable` | `--aipim-size-touch-comfortable` | 44px | Comfortable touch target (44px) |
| `size/icon.sm` | `--aipim-size-icon-sm` | 16px | Icon next to small text, in a small button or a tag |
| `size/icon.md` | `--aipim-size-icon-md` | 20px | Default icon size |
| `size/icon.lg` | `--aipim-size-icon-lg` | 24px | Icon in a top bar or a tab bar |
| `size/control.sm` | `--aipim-size-control-sm` | 32px | Height of a small button |
| `size/control.md` | `--aipim-size-control-md` | 40px | Height of a button and of a field |
| `size/control.lg` | `--aipim-size-control-lg` | 48px | Height of a large button and a large field |

## Breakpoints

| Token | Value |
|---|---|
| `breakpoint/tablet` | 600px |
| `breakpoint/desktop` | 1024px |
| `breakpoint/wide` | 1440px |

Mobile is below 600px. CSS custom properties cannot be used in a media query, so write the pixel value in the query.

## Elevation

| Token | Light | Dark | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `elevation/resting` (`--aipim-shadow-resting`) | 0px 1px 2px 0px rgba(26, 21, 17, 0.08), 0px 1px 3px 0px rgba(26, 21, 17, 0.06) | 0px 1px 2px 0px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.4), 0px 1px 3px 0px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.3) | Cards at rest |
| `elevation/raised` (`--aipim-shadow-raised`) | 0px 4px 12px -2px rgba(26, 21, 17, 0.12), 0px 2px 4px -1px rgba(26, 21, 17, 0.06) | 0px 4px 12px -2px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5), 0px 2px 4px -1px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.3) | Hover on an interactive card, a scrolled top bar |
| `elevation/overlay` (`--aipim-shadow-overlay`) | 0px 16px 32px -8px rgba(26, 21, 17, 0.24), 0px 8px 16px -4px rgba(26, 21, 17, 0.12) | 0px 16px 32px -8px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.6), 0px 8px 16px -4px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.4) | Toasts and dialogs |

## Stacking order

| Token | CSS variable | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `z/base` | `--aipim-z-base` | 0 | Normal content |
| `z/sticky` | `--aipim-z-sticky` | 100 | Sticky headers and bars |
| `z/dropdown` | `--aipim-z-dropdown` | 200 | Menus and popovers |
| `z/overlay` | `--aipim-z-overlay` | 300 | Overlays that are not dialogs |
| `z/modal` | `--aipim-z-modal` | 400 | Modal panels when they are not in the browser top layer |
| `z/toast` | `--aipim-z-toast` | 500 | Toasts, above everything |

## Motion

| Token | CSS variable | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `duration/fast` | `--aipim-duration-fast` | 100ms | Hover and press feedback, a toast leaving |
| `duration/base` | `--aipim-duration-base` | 200ms | A toast entering, small changes of state |
| `duration/slow` | `--aipim-duration-slow` | 320ms | Large movements |
| `easing/standard` | `--aipim-ease-standard` | cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1) | Most transitions |
| `easing/enter` | `--aipim-ease-enter` | cubic-bezier(0.05, 0.7, 0.1, 1) | Things that appear |
| `easing/exit` | `--aipim-ease-exit` | cubic-bezier(0.3, 0, 0.8, 0.15) | Things that leave |

With `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the generated CSS sets every duration to 0ms, so components that use the tokens stop animating with no extra code.

## Opacity

| Token | CSS variable | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `opacity/disabled` | `--aipim-opacity-disabled` | 0.4 | A disabled control |
| `opacity/scrim` | `--aipim-opacity-scrim` | 0.5 | The scrim behind a dialog |

## Rules

- Touch targets are at least 24px (`size/touch-min`) and 44px (`size/touch-comfortable`) wherever touch is the main input.
- Focus ring: 3px (`border/thick`), 3px away (`focus/offset`), visible for keyboard focus only.
- Disabled is 40% opacity (`opacity/disabled`) and is exempt from contrast, but keeps a label.
- Use tokens, never loose values. If a size has no token, the spec says so.


---

# Tutorial for designers

*Tutorial 1 of 3 · Designers*

You will turn a short brief into a screen made only from Aipim parts, and hand it to a developer who has no basic questions left.

## Choose your tutorial

Three tutorials, six steps each. Pick the one for how you work, and come back to the others when you need them.

| Tutorial | For | Where | File |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Design a screen (you are here) | Designers | In Figma | `docs/en/tutorials-designers.md` |
| 2. Build the frame | Developers | In HTML and CSS | `docs/en/tutorials-developers.md` |
| 3. Build with an agent | AI | With any coding agent | `docs/en/tutorials-ai.md` |

## Where this fits

The workflow has six stages. The designer tutorial covers the first four. The developer and AI tutorials cover the last two. The whole team joins the review and the release.

You lead stages 1, 2 and 4: frame the problem, design with the system and hand off. You join the review in stage 3.

| Stage | Name | Where it is covered |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Frame | **This tutorial: step 2** |
| 2 | Design | **This tutorial: steps 3 to 5** |
| 3 | Review | The whole team |
| 4 | Hand off | **This tutorial: step 6** |
| 5 | Build | Tutorial 2 or 3 |
| 6 | Verify and release | Tutorials 2 and 3, then the team |

If you are a stakeholder, you do not need a tutorial. You write the brief with the designer (stage 1), review in the Figma file, not in slides (stage 3), and accept the result against the brief (stage 6).

## The six steps: Design a screen

**You need**

- The Aipim DS file in Figma
- An idea of who the screen is for
- A developer or an AI agent who will build it

**You will have**

- A one-page brief
- A screen in light and dark, with every state
- A frame marked Ready for dev

### Step 1: Open the file and find your parts

Open Aipim DS in Figma (its pages are named in Portuguese). The Visão geral dos componentes page (Components overview) lists every part, grouped as Átomos, Moléculas and Organismos. The Telas de exemplo page (Example screens) has four whole screens you can duplicate and start from.

**Done when** you can name two components you will use.

### Step 2: Write the brief

Four lines, in your own words. Who is it for? What changes for them? How will you know it worked? What limits you: platform, deadline, accessibility. Agree on it with the stakeholder before you draw.

**Done when** the stakeholder says the brief is right.

### Step 3: Start from what already exists

Ask first: does a component or a pattern already solve this? Use it. Would a small change solve it, like a new variant? Propose it. Ask for a new component only when you need it in more than one place.

**Done when** you have a list of parts and no custom drawings.

### Step 4: Build with instances and variables

Drag components from the Library (page Componentes) into your frame and keep them as instances: never detach. For color, space, radius and text, pick variables and text styles. Never type a hex value or a loose number.

**Done when** every layer comes from the system.

### Step 5: Design every state, in light and dark

Show the screen empty, loading, with an error and with success, and add a long-text case. Then set the frame to the Dark mode and look again. Write like a person, warm and to the point. An error says what happened and what to do, and a button starts with a verb.

**Done when** both themes look right and no text is cut.

### Step 6: Hand it off

Mark the frame Ready for dev and link it in the ticket. List the components you used: the Figma name is the class name, so Button is aipim-button. Flag what is custom, and note the behavior, the focus order and the labels.

**Done when** a developer can start without asking basic questions.

### Final check

Tick every line before you move on.

- [ ] Only Library components, no detached instances
- [ ] Only variables, no loose colors or sizes
- [ ] Light and dark checked
- [ ] Every state and a long-text case designed
- [ ] Copy follows the Aipim voice: warm and direct
- [ ] Focus order and labels noted

## Keep these close

Two short lists that help in every tutorial: the same names in Figma and in code, and what to do when the system has no part for what you need.

### Same names everywhere

| In Figma | In code |
|---|---|
| Component Button | Class aipim-button, and the spec docs/en/components/button.md |
| Variable bg/surface | --aipim-bg-surface |
| Text style Aipim/h4 | --aipim-text-h4-* |
| Icon close | #aipim-close in icons/sprite.svg |

### Need something new? Ask in this order

1. Does a component or a pattern already solve it? Use it.
2. Does a small change solve it, such as a variant? Propose it.
3. Is it needed in more than one place? Request a new component.
4. Only needed here? Build it in your product with Aipim tokens, and keep it out of the system.

Stuck? Raise it before you build a custom version.


---

# Tutorial for developers

*Tutorial 2 of 3 · Developers*

You will take a frame marked Ready for dev and build it in HTML and CSS, using Aipim as it is.

## Choose your tutorial

Three tutorials, six steps each. Pick the one for how you work, and come back to the others when you need them.

| Tutorial | For | Where | File |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Design a screen | Designers | In Figma | `docs/en/tutorials-designers.md` |
| 2. Build the frame (you are here) | Developers | In HTML and CSS | `docs/en/tutorials-developers.md` |
| 3. Build with an agent | AI | With any coding agent | `docs/en/tutorials-ai.md` |

## Where this fits

The workflow has six stages. The designer tutorial covers the first four. The developer and AI tutorials cover the last two. The whole team joins the review and the release.

You lead stage 5, the build, and join the review in stage 3 and the release in stage 6.

| Stage | Name | Where it is covered |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Frame | Tutorial 1, step 2 |
| 2 | Design | Tutorial 1, steps 3 to 5 |
| 3 | Review | The whole team |
| 4 | Hand off | Tutorial 1, step 6 |
| 5 | Build | **This tutorial: steps 1 to 5** |
| 6 | Verify and release | **This tutorial: step 6** |

## The six steps: Build the frame

**You need**

- A frame marked Ready for dev
- A web project, in any stack
- Aipim, from npm or from GitHub

**You will have**

- A pull request that matches the frame
- A screen that works in light and dark, with the keyboard and at 200% zoom

### Step 1: Get Aipim into your project

Install the package from npm, or copy the folder from GitHub. Everything you need is then inside node_modules/aipim-ds.

*Terminal*

```bash
npm install aipim-ds
```

**Done when** the folders tokens/build/css and components/web exist in the package.

### Step 2: Load the fonts, the tokens and the components

Add these lines to the head of your page, in this order. The components read the tokens, so the tokens come first. The script is optional: it adds tab keys, dismiss buttons and dialog commands. Then set the page colors: the background with --aipim-bg-canvas and the text with --aipim-text-primary.

*In the head of your page*

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Antonio:wght@600;700&family=Karla:wght@400;700&display=swap">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="node_modules/aipim-ds/tokens/build/css/aipim.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="node_modules/aipim-ds/components/web/aipim-components.css">
<script src="node_modules/aipim-ds/components/web/aipim.js"></script>
```

**Done when** the page has the Aipim background and Karla text.

### Step 3: Read the frame and the specs

Open the frame and read the hand-off note. For each component on the list, open its spec in docs/en/components, like button.md. The spec has the markup, the states and the accessibility notes.

**Done when** you know every component and its states.

### Step 4: Copy the markup and use only tokens

Copy the markup from the spec. Use native elements: button for actions, a for links, input with a real label. For color and space use --aipim-* variables. Never write a hex value.

*Markup from the spec*

```html
<button class="aipim-button" type="button">Save changes</button>
```

**Done when** nothing in your code is a hex value.

### Step 5: Customize through variables

Need another size or color? Set the component’s own variables, such as --aipim-button-height. Never use !important and never rewrite the component’s CSS. Your brand’s fonts work the same way: load them in place of Antonio and Karla, then set --aipim-font-heading and --aipim-font-body on :root.

*In your CSS*

```css
.toolbar .aipim-button { --aipim-button-height: var(--aipim-size-control-lg); }
```

**Done when** the change lives in variables and the component CSS is untouched.

### Step 6: Test it and open the pull request

Test light and dark: add data-theme="dark" to the html element. Then use only the keyboard: every control must be reachable and show a focus ring. Zoom to 200%. Run an automated check such as axe. Open the pull request and link the Figma frame.

*Dark theme*

```html
<html data-theme="dark">
```

**Done when** the checks pass and the pull request links the frame.

### Final check

Tick every line before you move on.

- [ ] Only --aipim-* variables, no hex
- [ ] Native elements, a visible focus ring and a label on every control
- [ ] Keyboard only works, and 200% zoom does not break the layout
- [ ] Light, dark and reduced motion checked
- [ ] The pull request links the Figma frame

## How the system is built

Why Aipim works the way it does, and how it checks itself.

### Copy the code or install a package

*Decided*

- Components: copied into the project, so the developer owns the code
- Tokens: the CSS files, and the npm package aipim-ds
- No hidden tracking: the licenses ask for credit and nothing more

### tokens.json generates everything

*One source, many destinations*

- CSS variables, Jetpack Compose, SwiftUI, an import bundle for Figma and the color, type and space docs
- Tool: tools/build_tokens.py, which writes tokens.json in the W3C 2025.10 format

### Automatic verification

*Check*

- tools/build_tokens.py: contrast and color blindness checks, and it fails if a pair fails
- tools/build_web.py --check: the component stylesheet is up to date
- tools/build_ai.py --check: llms.txt, llms-full.txt and AGENTS.md are up to date
- tools/build_tutorials.py --check: the tutorials are up to date

### Try it now

*Shortcuts*

- Open components/web/examples/index.html: every component, with a light and dark toggle
- Copy a snippet from the spec of each component
- Starters for Vite and Next are on the roadmap (ROADMAP.md)

## Web components and the repository

The conventions every component follows, and where everything lives.

### Not tied to a framework

*Conventions*

- HTML and CSS
- Only semantic tokens, never loose values
- --aipim-* variables per component as an escape hatch
- No !important

### By classes and ARIA attributes

*Variants and states*

- By classes and ARIA attributes
- Usage and customization example per component

### Repository structure

*Folders*

- docs/ and docs/en/components/
- tokens/ (tokens.json and build/)
- components/web/ and icons/
- tools/ (generators and checks)
- AGENTS.md, llms.txt and llms-full.txt

## Versions and platforms

How updates reach you, and what comes after the web.

### Versioning and updating

*Versions*

- Semver: major breaks, minor adds, patch fixes
- Changelog in each version

### Deprecation and migration

*Breaking changes*

- Deprecation notice before removing
- Step-by-step migration notes

### Native tokens

*Today*

- Theme for Compose and SwiftUI generated from the tokens, not yet tested in an app

### Native components

*Later*

- Compose and SwiftUI components are on the roadmap, if Aipim gets traction

## Keep these close

Two short lists that help in every tutorial: the same names in Figma and in code, and what to do when the system has no part for what you need.

### Same names everywhere

| In Figma | In code |
|---|---|
| Component Button | Class aipim-button, and the spec docs/en/components/button.md |
| Variable bg/surface | --aipim-bg-surface |
| Text style Aipim/h4 | --aipim-text-h4-* |
| Icon close | #aipim-close in icons/sprite.svg |

### Need something new? Ask in this order

1. Does a component or a pattern already solve it? Use it.
2. Does a small change solve it, such as a variant? Propose it.
3. Is it needed in more than one place? Request a new component.
4. Only needed here? Build it in your product with Aipim tokens, and keep it out of the system.

Stuck? Raise it before you build a custom version.

# Tutorial for AI agents

*Tutorial 3 of 3 · AI*

You will brief an AI coding agent so it builds with Aipim, and then review its work before it ships. The agent builds. People decide and review.

## Choose your tutorial

Three tutorials, six steps each. Pick the one for how you work, and come back to the others when you need them.

| Tutorial | For | Where | File |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Design a screen | Designers | In Figma | `docs/en/tutorials-designers.md` |
| 2. Build the frame | Developers | In HTML and CSS | `docs/en/tutorials-developers.md` |
| 3. Build with an agent (you are here) | AI | With any coding agent | `docs/en/tutorials-ai.md` |

## Where this fits

The workflow has six stages. The designer tutorial covers the first four. The developer and AI tutorials cover the last two. The whole team joins the review and the release.

The agent works in stage 5, the build. You review its work and decide, and the team joins stage 6.

| Stage | Name | Where it is covered |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Frame | Tutorial 1, step 2 |
| 2 | Design | Tutorial 1, steps 3 to 5 |
| 3 | Review | The whole team |
| 4 | Hand off | Tutorial 1, step 6 |
| 5 | Build | **This tutorial: steps 1 to 4** |
| 6 | Verify and release | **This tutorial: steps 5 and 6** |

## The six steps: Build with an agent

**You need**

- An AI coding agent that can read the files of your project
- Aipim in your project (tutorial 2, step 1)
- The brief and the Figma link (tutorial 1)

**You will have**

- A screen built only from Aipim parts
- A reviewed change you can trust

### Step 1: Put Aipim within the agent’s reach

Install Aipim in the project. The package carries AGENTS.md, the file that tells an agent how to build with Aipim. Many agents read it on their own. If yours does not, copy it to the root of your project.

*Terminal*

```bash
cp node_modules/aipim-ds/AGENTS.md .
```

**Done when** the agent can open AGENTS.md.

### Step 2: Give it three things

The brief, the Figma link and AGENTS.md. If your agent works better with one file, give it llms-full.txt: the whole system in one place. llms.txt is the short index.

**Done when** all three are in the project or in the conversation.

### Step 3: Ask for a plan first

Do not let it write code yet. A plan costs a minute and catches wrong turns early.

*Prompt*

```text
Read AGENTS.md. Here is the brief and the Figma frame: [paste both]. Before you write code, list the Aipim components you will use and anything that does not fit the system.
```

**Done when** you read the plan and agree with it.

### Step 4: Ask it to build, with the rules

Say the rules out loud, even though AGENTS.md has them. Short and specific beats long and vague.

*Prompt*

```text
Build the screen with Aipim components and --aipim-* tokens only. Read the spec of every component you use. No hex values, no !important, native elements, a visible focus ring. Then run the checks in AGENTS.md, under Verify, and tell me what they showed.
```

**Done when** the agent says which checks it ran and what they showed.

### Step 5: Review it like a pull request

Do not trust it blindly. Open the diff and the screen. Search for hex values and !important. Look for a label on every field and an aria-label on every button that has only an icon. Test with the keyboard, in light and dark.

**Done when** you could explain every change in the diff.

### Step 6: Correct with specific feedback

Name the file, the line and the rule, then ask the agent to run the checks again. When it passes your review, open the pull request and link the Figma frame.

*Prompt*

```text
Line 24 of card.html uses #ffffff. Use var(--aipim-bg-surface) instead, then run the checks again.
```

**Done when** a person approved the pull request.

### Final check

Tick every line before you move on.

- [ ] The agent had the brief, the Figma link and AGENTS.md
- [ ] It listed its components before it wrote code
- [ ] No hex, no !important, no custom copy of a component
- [ ] Every control works with the keyboard, in light and dark
- [ ] You read the diff, and a person approved the pull request

## How the docs are written

The goal is an agent that gets it right the first time.

### An agent that gets it right the first time

*Goal*

- The agent reads Aipim and generates correct, accessible screens without human help
- Aipim’s third audience, next to designers and developers

### How the docs are written

*Principles*

- One source of truth: tokens.json
- Explicit rules, with concrete values
- One fact in one place
- Tested examples
- Short files, with frontmatter

## The Markdown package

The files an agent reads, and how a spec is shaped.

### llms.txt and llms-full.txt

*Indexes for LLMs*

- llms.txt: a short index, with one link and one line per document
- llms-full.txt: all documents together, to paste whole into the context
- Generated by tools/build_ai.py from the specs

### AGENTS.md

*Rules for agents*

- What Aipim is, the 12 rules, setup, the patterns that are easy to get wrong and how to verify
- A Claude skill that says when and how to apply Aipim is on the roadmap

### Foundations and specs

*Base documents*

- Color, typography, and space, shape and motion: generated from tokens.json
- One spec per component, with the same sections
- Flow patterns are on the roadmap

### Component spec in Markdown

*Template*

- Frontmatter: name, description, status, group, html, class, css, figma, wcag, related
- Tokens used, WCAG criteria, related components
- Fixed sections, always in the same order: when to use, when not to use, variants and props, states, tokens used, accessibility, code examples, do and don’t
- See docs/en/components/button.md for a real example

## Use it with your agent

Where to put the files in the tools people use most.

### Import AGENTS.md

*Claude Code*

- Copy AGENTS.md into the project and import it from CLAUDE.md with @AGENTS.md
- Point the agent to llms-full.txt when it needs the specs

### Read it from the root

*Cursor and Copilot*

- Most agent tools read AGENTS.md from the root of the project
- If yours does not, point an editor rule to the file

### Things to ask

*Example prompts*

- “Build a login screen with Aipim”
- “Change the brand color and validate the contrast”
- “Add an empty state to this list”

## What comes next, and a caveat

On the roadmap (ROADMAP.md), and what is still not guaranteed.

### MCP server

*On the roadmap*

- Tools: get_tokens, get_component(name), check_contrast(fg, bg)
- The agent queries instead of guessing

### Test suite (evals)

*Differentiator*

- Test requests and automatic checks: uses only tokens? passes contrast? has visible focus?
- Publishes the result: how well agents use Aipim

### What is still not guaranteed

*Caveat*

- llms.txt is not read by every tool
- The real value is in the whole: structured docs, AGENTS.md, the skill, MCP and tests

# Voice and microcopy

How the words in an Aipim interface sound, and how to write the small texts: buttons, labels, helper text, errors, empty states and dialogs. The components do not set any text for you, so this is the part that is up to the person writing the screen.

## Voice

Aipim talks like a helpful person who respects your time.

- **Warm.** Talk to one person. Say "you". Be kind without being cute.
- **Direct.** Say the most important thing first. Short sentences. One idea per message.
- **Plain.** Use the words people use. If a word needs explaining, pick a different word.
- **Honest.** Say what happened and what is not possible. Do not hide a limit behind a cheerful tone.

What it is not: formal ("Kindly be advised") or full of exclamation marks, and never playful at the wrong moment. Save celebration for moments that earn it, like finishing something hard.

## Rules that apply everywhere

1. **Sentence case.** "Save changes", not "Save Changes". Product and proper names keep their capitals.
2. **Start with the verb on actions.** "Add member", "Download report". The label says what will happen.
3. **Never "OK", "Yes" or "Submit" alone.** Say the action: "Delete project", "Send message". The same label should make sense without the text around it, because screen reader users often hear buttons and links on their own.
4. **Say what to do, not what went wrong with the person.** "Enter an email like name@example.com", not "Invalid input".
5. **No blame.** "We could not save your changes", not "You made a mistake". Do not say "sorry" unless something on our side failed.
6. **Do not say "please" before every instruction.** Use it once if it softens a real request.
7. **Numbers and dates the way people say them.** "3 unread", "Today, 14:30". Use numerals for counts.
8. **No jargon and no internal names.** "Your session ended", not "Error 401".
9. **Do not build sentences from pieces.** Whole sentences translate and read aloud better than a label glued to a number.
10. **Keep it short, but not cryptic.** Cut a word only if the meaning stays.

## By component

| Component | Write it like this | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **Button** | Verb, then object. Two or three words. | "Add member" |
| **Icon button** | No visible text, so the `aria-label` names the action. | `aria-label="Close"` |
| **Link** | Say where it goes. Never "click here" or "read more" alone. | "Read the accessibility notes" |
| **Text field label** | Say what to enter. Keep it above the field, always visible. | "Email" |
| **Helper text** | The format or the reason, not a repeat of the label. | "Used only for receipts" |
| **Error text** | What is wrong and how to fix it, in one sentence. | "Enter a valid email" |
| **Checkbox, radio, switch** | The option itself, positive and specific. For a switch, say what turns on. | "Email notifications" |
| **Alert** | Optional title (two to five words) and one or two sentences. | "Check your card and try again." |
| **Toast** | One short sentence about what just happened. Past tense. | "Item saved." |
| **Empty state** | A title that says what is empty, one sentence about what to do. | "Nothing here yet" |
| **Modal** | The title names the action or asks the question. The buttons repeat the action. | "Delete project?" with "Cancel" and "Delete project" |
| **Tabs and tab bar** | One or two words. Nouns. | "Overview", "Messages" |
| **Tag** | One or two words. | "Design" |
| **Top bar** | The name of where you are. | "Settings" |

## Four kinds of message

**Error.** What happened, then what to do. If you cannot say how to fix it, say what you will do about it.
- Do: "We could not save your changes. Check your connection and try again."
- Don't: "Error: operation failed."

**Success.** Confirm what was done, briefly. A toast is enough. Do not celebrate routine actions.
- Do: "Item saved."
- Don't: "Awesome! Your item has been successfully saved!"

**Empty.** Say why it is empty and give the next step. Do not apologize for being empty.
- Do: "No projects yet. Create your first project to see it here."
- Don't: "Oops! Nothing to see."

**Confirmation.** Say what will happen and, when it cannot be undone, say so.
- Do: "Delete project? This cannot be undone. All files in the project will be removed."
- Don't: "Are you sure?"

## Accessible text

- Every icon-only control has an `aria-label` that names the action, in the same words you would put on a visible button.
- Links and buttons make sense out of context (see rule 3).
- Do not use color words or position alone: "the red button" and "the field on the right" do not work for everyone. Name the control.
- Status messages go in an element with `role="status"` (or `role="alert"` for errors), so assistive technology reads them. See the Alert and Toast specs.
- Write plain language. A reading level most adults handle easily is a good target for anything people must act on.

## Words to avoid

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| "Utilize" | "Use" |
| "Click here" | A link that says where it goes |
| Invalid, illegal | What is expected: "Enter a date like 12/05/2026" |
| Failed | What did not happen: "We could not send your message" |
| Whoops, oops | Say what happened |
| Are you sure? | State the consequence |

## Translation

Aipim's own texts are written in English and in Brazilian Portuguese (the Storybook has both, and the Portuguese docs are in `docs/pt-br`). When you translate a product:
- Keep strings whole, with no sentence assembled from parts, because word order changes.
- Leave room: many languages are 30% longer. Components wrap long text instead of cutting it, so labels can grow.
- Plurals and numbers follow the language's rules. Use your i18n library's plural support, not "item(s)".

# Verification

What has been checked on the web components, how, and when. Run `python3 tools/verify_web.py` to repeat it.

**Last verified: 2026-10-30**, in Chromium 148, WebKit 26.4 and Firefox 150 with axe-core 4.14.0, on `components/web/examples/index.html`.

## What passes

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Automatic accessibility (axe-core), light and dark theme, in Chromium, WebKit and Firefox | No violations |
| Forced colors (emulated: `forced-colors: active`) in the three engines | Same checks pass (without the contrast rule, which the system palette decides); every control and container keeps a visible edge, and the selected tab keeps its bar |
| Palette contrast (`tools/build_tokens.py`) | 88 contrast checks, 0 failures, plus color blindness simulation. Links must also stand out from the body text (color difference of at least 20) |
| Theme builder (`tools/verify_theme_builder.py`) | With the default colors, the same 57 tones and 82 role colors as `tokens/tokens.json`. A brand color whose pairs fail for color blindness is fixed by tone alone, and suggestions on 200 random themes pass and keep the status colors in their family. The page has no axe violations in light and dark, nor with problems marked and the confirmation open; "See as" filters the preview and counts the problems per kind of vision; a problem in the list leads to its mark, whose tooltip (by pointer or keyboard, closed by Escape) says the same, and a second click makes it blink; exporting a theme with problems asks once and writes the problems into the file |
| Keyboard: tabs (arrows, Home, End), dismiss with Enter, modal open and Escape | Works |
| Brazilian field: the mask while typing and on a value that came with the page, Backspace on a dot or a dash, the check when leaving (CPF, CNPJ with letters, phone, date), the error cleared as soon as the value is valid, an error from the server kept when the person only passes by | Works |
| Select and combobox: the prompt of the select in a muted color; the combobox filtering without caring for accents, Down and Up opening and wrapping, Enter and a click choosing (with focus kept in the field and the value stored), Escape closing and then clearing, the empty message and the count read by a screen reader, the error when leaving with a text that is not an option, a name typed in full taken as the option. What a screen reader reads aloud is still to be checked by hand | Works |
| Date picker: the button hidden until the script is ready and disabled with its field, the calendar opening on the date in the field (or today), the arrows, Home, Page Down and Shift+Page Up, a day outside the limits that cannot be chosen, Tab kept inside the calendar, Escape and a choice putting focus back on the button, a click outside closing it, the range error on leaving and while the date is still outside, the day of the week shown only for a valid date inside the limits, axe on the open calendar. What a screen reader reads aloud is still to be checked by hand | Works |
| Avatar, list item and accordion: the avatar sizes (32, 40, 48) and the overlap of the group (6, 8, 12), the ring of the group, a row with title and description at 69px and a row with only a title at 48px, hover only on the row that acts, the focus ring inside a link row, a disabled link out of the keyboard and the clicks, a click and Space on the row with a switch, the accordion opening and closing with a click, Enter and Space, one item open at a time with the same `name`, the chevron turned up. What a screen reader reads aloud is still to be checked by hand | Works |
| 200% browser zoom (640 CSS px wide) | No horizontal scroll, no text cut off |
| Reflow at 320 CSS px (400% zoom) | No horizontal scroll |
| Root font size at 200% (a large browser text setting) | No horizontal scroll, text wraps instead of being cut |
| Text spacing from WCAG 1.4.12 (line height 1.5, letter spacing 0.12em, word spacing 0.16em, paragraph spacing 2em) | No text cut off |

## Known limits

- **Touch targets.** The Button small and medium sizes, the standalone link, the small icon button, and the dismiss and remove buttons are smaller than 44px. They meet the WCAG 2.2 AA minimum of 24px (2.5.8), not the 44px comfortable size. Use the large Button and the medium icon button where touch matters.
- **Text fields.** A value longer than the field scrolls inside it, as any native input does.
- **Not tested yet.** Real screen readers (VoiceOver, NVDA, TalkBack), the Safari app itself (WebKit is tested through Playwright), and the real Windows high contrast mode (forced colors is only emulated). The components use native elements and ARIA as documented in each spec, but they have not been tried with these tools.

## How it is checked

`tools/verify_web.py` serves the gallery, loads it in a browser engine through Playwright (Chromium by default; `--browser webkit` or `--browser firefox` for the others, and `--forced-colors` for forced colors), runs axe-core in both themes, drives the keyboard checks, and loads the page at four sizes and settings, looking for horizontal page scroll and for text that escapes its own box. It exits with an error if any check fails. The CI workflow runs it on every push, in the three engines and in forced colors.

When you change a component, run it again and update the date above.
