<!-- docs/en/components/avatar.md · class aipim-avatar · WCAG ["1.1.1 Non-text Content", "1.3.1 Info and Relationships", "1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum)", "1.4.11 Non-text Contrast"] -->
# Avatar

A person or a thing inside a circle: a photo, the initials on a tone, or an icon. It gives a face to a list, a comment or a group.

## When to use

- To show who a person is, or what an item is, in a list, a comment or a card.
- To show how many people take part, with the group and its count ("+3").

## When not to use

- Only to decorate. If the avatar does not say who it is, leave it out.
- For the icon of an action: use the [icon button](icon-button.md).
- For a number or a status on top of an icon: use the [badge](badge.md).

## Decision: photo, initials or icon

The avatar draws what it receives. Whoever builds the screen chooses: the photo when there is one, the initials when there is only a name, the icon when there is neither. Aipim does not make that choice for you.

## Decision: four tones, with the text of the tone

The initials sit on one of the four tones of the system (salmon, blue, yellow and green), always with the text of the tone (`tint/text`), which the token generator checks. Aipim does not pick the tone: use the same one for the same person on every screen, and a long list gets color without looking random.

## Variants and props

| Class or attribute | What it does |
|---|---|
| `aipim-avatar` | The circle, 40px. Without a tone it is `bg/sunken`, for the icon, the photo space and the count. |
| `aipim-avatar--sm`, `aipim-avatar--lg` | 32px and 48px. The small one writes the initials in the overline style and draws a 16px icon. |
| `aipim-avatar--primary`, `--secondary`, `--tertiary`, `--success` | The tone behind the initials. |
| `img` inside | The photo. It fills the circle. |
| `svg.aipim-icon` inside | The icon, `aria-hidden="true"`. |
| `aipim-avatar-group` | A row of avatars that overlap, each one with a 3px ring in the color of the page. Put `role="group"` and an `aria-label` on it. |
| `aipim-avatar-group--sm`, `--lg` | Sizes the avatars inside and sets the overlap: 6, 8 (default) and 12px. |

## States

The avatar only shows. It has no hover, focus or disabled state. When it sits inside a link or a button, the state belongs to that link or button.

## Tokens used

| Applies to | State | Token | Light | Dark |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Initials background | Primary | `tint/primary` | #FEBBA9 | #892402 |
| Initials background | Secondary | `tint/secondary` | #AED1FE | #014B95 |
| Initials background | Tertiary | `tint/tertiary` | #FFD337 | #5E4B03 |
| Initials background | Success | `tint/success` | #A0DFB5 | #025D33 |
| Initials text | All four | `tint/text` | #1A1511 | #FDF9F6 |
| Background | Icon, photo, count | `bg/sunken` | #ECE5DF | #0E0A07 |
| Icon | Icon | `text/secondary` | #4A423C | #ECE5DF |
| Count text | Count | `text/primary` | #1A1511 | #FDF9F6 |
| Group ring | Group | `bg/surface` | #FDF9F6 | #302A25 |

| Measure | Token | Small | Medium | Large |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Diameter | `size/control-sm`, `size/control-md`, `size/control-lg` | 32 | 40 | 48 |
| Icon | `size/icon-sm`, `size/icon-md` | 16 | 20 | 20 |
| Initials | `text/overline`, `text/label` | Overline | Label | Label |
| Overlap in a group | `space/8`, `space/12` | 6 (no token) | 8 | 12 |

| Measure | Token | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Corner | `radius/full` | Always a circle |
| Group ring | `border/thick` | 3 |

The overlap is a negative margin, since a token cannot be negative. The ring is drawn outside the circle and takes no room: a group of four medium avatars is 136px wide.

## Accessibility

- Tab does not stop on an avatar. Inside a link or a button, the focus goes to the link or the button.
- A photo is an `img` whose `alt` is the name of the person. When the name is written next to it, use an empty `alt`.
- Initials have `aria-hidden="true"` when the name is next to them. Alone, they take `role="img"` and an `aria-label` with the name.
- An icon is `aria-hidden="true"`: it is only decoration.
- A group has `role="group"` and an `aria-label` ("Participants"). The count carries a hidden text (`aipim-visually-hidden`) that completes it: "+3 more people".
- The initials use `tint/text` on each tone, a pair the token generator checks in light and dark.

## Code examples

```html
<span class="aipim-avatar aipim-avatar--primary" role="img" aria-label="Talis Galhardi">TG</span>

<span class="aipim-avatar"><img src="ana.jpg" alt="Ana Vieira"></span>

<span class="aipim-avatar" aria-hidden="true">
  <svg class="aipim-icon" aria-hidden="true"><use href="icons/sprite.svg#aipim-user"></use></svg>
</span>

<div class="aipim-avatar-group" role="group" aria-label="Participants">
  <span class="aipim-avatar aipim-avatar--primary" role="img" aria-label="Talis Galhardi">TG</span>
  <span class="aipim-avatar aipim-avatar--secondary" role="img" aria-label="Ana Vieira">AV</span>
  <span class="aipim-avatar aipim-avatar--success" role="img" aria-label="Lucas Ueda">LU</span>
  <span class="aipim-avatar">+3<span class="aipim-visually-hidden"> more people</span></span>
</div>
```

## Do and don't

- Do: show up to four avatars and sum up the rest in the count (+3).
- Don't: stack eight avatars, which turns the group into an unreadable strip.


---

<!-- docs/en/components/badge.md · class aipim-badge · WCAG ["1.1.1 Non-text Content", "1.3.1 Info and Relationships", "1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum)"] -->
# Badge

A small mark with a numeral or an icon, next to text. Decorative.

## When to use

- A step number next to the step it names ("1", "2", "3").
- An icon chip that gives a block a small visual anchor.
- Next to text that already says everything the badge shows.

## When not to use

- To carry information on its own, such as an unread count: write it as text.
- As a button or a link: it is not interactive. Use a [button](button.md) or a [link](link.md).
- For a category or a status: use a [tag](tag.md).

## Variants and props

| Class | What it does |
|---|---|
| `aipim-badge` | Outline, round, 48. A 2px border and the numeral or icon in `action/primary/bg`. |
| `aipim-badge--filled` | Filled with `action/primary/bg`, content in `action/primary/text`. |
| `aipim-badge--tint` | Filled with `tint/primary`, content in `tint/text`. |
| `aipim-badge--square` | Rounded square (`radius/md`) instead of a circle. |
| `aipim-badge--sm` | 32 instead of 48. |
| `aipim-badge > .aipim-icon` | An icon instead of a numeral: 24px, or 16px in the small size. |

## States

None. The badge is not interactive and cannot be focused.

## Tokens used

| Applies to | Style | Token | Light | Dark |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Border, numeral and icon | Outline | `action/primary/bg` | #B43000 | #FF9275 |
| Fill | Filled | `action/primary/bg` | #B43000 | #FF9275 |
| Numeral and icon | Filled | `action/primary/text` | #FDF9F6 | #1A1511 |
| Fill | Tint | `tint/primary` | #FEBBA9 | #892402 |
| Numeral and icon | Tint | `tint/text` | #1A1511 | #FDF9F6 |

| Measure | Token | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Size, default | `size/control-lg` | 48 |
| Size, small | `size/control-sm` | 32 |
| Icon size, default | `size/icon-lg` | 24 |
| Icon size, small | `size/icon-sm` | 16 |
| Corner radius, round | `radius/full` | Fully round |
| Corner radius, square | `radius/md` | 8 |
| Border width (outline) | `border/medium` | 2 |
| Numeral type | `Aipim/label` | 16/20 Bold |

Sizes are measured from the outer edge. In code the border is 2px on the outline style and transparent on the others, so all three styles are the same size.

## Accessibility

- A badge is decorative: put `aria-hidden="true"` on it. The text next to it carries the meaning, so a screen reader reads "Create the file", not "1 Create the file".
- Never use a badge as the only way to give information. A numeral without text, such as an unread count, must also be written as text.
- Contrast of the numeral or icon against the badge, light and dark: outline 5.58:1 on the page background (8.30:1 in dark), filled 5.96:1 (8.30:1 in dark), tint 11.12:1 (8.66:1 in dark). The shape of a tint badge is decoration, not information, so it needs no contrast against the page.
- The numeral uses `Aipim/label`, 16px, so it meets the minimum body size.

## Code examples

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="aipim.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="aipim-components.css">

<!-- A step number next to its text -->
<div style="display:flex;align-items:center;gap:12px">
  <span class="aipim-badge" aria-hidden="true">1</span>
  <span>Create the file</span>
</div>

<!-- Filled, square, small, with an icon -->
<span class="aipim-badge aipim-badge--filled aipim-badge--square aipim-badge--sm" aria-hidden="true">
  <svg class="aipim-icon" aria-hidden="true"><use href="icons/sprite.svg#aipim-search"></use></svg>
</span>
```

## Do and don't

- Do: put a badge next to text that says the same thing, with `aria-hidden="true"`.
- Don't: use a badge alone to show information, such as a count nobody can read out.


---

<!-- docs/en/components/button.md · class aipim-button · WCAG ["1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum)", "1.4.11 Non-text Contrast", "2.4.7 Focus Visible", "2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum)", "4.1.2 Name, Role, Value"] -->
# Button

The main action of a screen or block.

## When to use

- For the main action of a screen or block.
- One primary button per screen.
- Use secondary, outline or ghost for the other actions.

## When not to use

- To go to another page: use a [link](link.md).
- Several actions of equal weight side by side: keep one primary and make the rest quieter.
- Destructive actions: not covered in v1.0.

## Variants and props

| Class | What it does |
|---|---|
| `aipim-button` | Primary. The main action. |
| `aipim-button--secondary` | Secondary color fill. |
| `aipim-button--outline` | Transparent with a 2px border. |
| `aipim-button--ghost` | Transparent, no border. |
| `aipim-button--sm` / default / `aipim-button--lg` | Heights 32, 40 and 48px. |
| `aipim-button__icon-leading` | Put on an icon before the label. It is replaced by the spinner while loading. |
| `aipim-button__spinner` | A `loading` icon, shown only while `aria-busy="true"`. |

A label, optionally with one icon before or after it. Icon-only buttons are not part of v1.0.

## States

Default, hover, focus, disabled and loading. Pressed looks like hover.

- **Disabled:** the native `disabled` attribute (or `aria-disabled="true"` on a link styled as a button). Opacity is `opacity/disabled` (40%).
- **Loading:** set `aria-busy="true"` and show the spinner. The label stays. Ignore activation in your code while it is busy: the CSS also blocks the pointer.
- **Focus:** a 3px ring in `focus/ring`, 3px away from the button (`focus/offset`). It shows for keyboard focus only (`:focus-visible`).

## Tokens used

| Applies to | State | Token | Light | Dark |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Primary fill | Default | `action/primary/bg` | #B43000 | #FF9275 |
| Primary fill | Hover, pressed | `action/primary/hover` | #892402 | #FEBBA9 |
| Primary label and icons | All | `action/primary/text` | #FDF9F6 | #1A1511 |
| Secondary fill | Default | `action/secondary/bg` | #0364C2 | #8CBEFE |
| Secondary fill | Hover, pressed | `action/secondary/hover` | #014B95 | #AED1FE |
| Secondary label and icons | All | `action/secondary/text` | #FDF9F6 | #1A1511 |
| Outline border, outline and ghost label | All | `action/secondary/bg` | #0364C2 | #8CBEFE |
| Outline and ghost fill | Hover, pressed | `bg/sunken` | #ECE5DF | #0E0A07 |
| Focus ring | Focus | `focus/ring` | #0364C2 | #AED1FE |
| Whole button | Disabled | `opacity/disabled` | 40% | 40% |

| Measure | Token | Small | Medium | Large |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Height | `size/control-sm`, `-md`, `-lg` | 32 | 40 | 48 |
| Horizontal padding | `space-role/inset-sm`, `-md`, `-lg` | 12 | 16 | 24 |
| Gap between icon and label | `space/8` | 8 | 8 | 8 |
| Icon size | `size/icon-sm`, `size/icon-md` | 16 | 20 | 20 |
| Corner radius | `radius/md` | 8 | 8 | 8 |
| Border width (outline) | `border/medium` | 2 | 2 | 2 |
| Label type | `Aipim/label` | 16/20 Bold | 16/20 Bold | 16/20 Bold |

Sizes are measured from the outer edge. In code the border is always 2px (transparent on filled and ghost buttons), so every variant has the same size and the label never moves.

Heights 32 and 40 are below the 44px comfortable touch target (`size/touch-comfortable`) and meet the 24px minimum (`size/touch-min`). Use Large where touch is the main input.

## Accessibility

- Use the native `button` element. Enter and Space activate it.
- Tab moves focus, and the ring is always visible.
- A disabled button leaves the tab order (native `disabled`).
- Loading: `aria-busy="true"` and keep the label text.
- A button that only shows an icon needs an `aria-label`.
- A toggle button needs `aria-pressed`.

## Code examples

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="aipim.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="button.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="aipim-base.css"> <!-- for .aipim-icon -->

<button class="aipim-button" type="button">Save</button>
<button class="aipim-button aipim-button--outline" type="button">Cancel</button>

<!-- Icon before the label -->
<button class="aipim-button" type="button">
  <svg class="aipim-icon aipim-button__icon-leading" aria-hidden="true"><use href="icons/sprite.svg#aipim-add"></use></svg>
  <span>Add</span>
</button>

<!-- Loading -->
<button class="aipim-button" type="button" aria-busy="true">
  <svg class="aipim-icon aipim-button__spinner" aria-hidden="true"><use href="icons/sprite.svg#aipim-loading"></use></svg>
  <span>Saving</span>
</button>
```

## Do and don't

- Do: one primary action, the other is quieter (Save primary, Cancel outline).
- Don't: two primary buttons side by side, they compete for attention.


---

<!-- docs/en/components/checkbox.md · class aipim-checkbox · WCAG ["1.3.1 Info and Relationships", "1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum)", "1.4.11 Non-text Contrast", "2.4.7 Focus Visible", "2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum)", "4.1.2 Name, Role, Value"] -->
# Checkbox

Lets a person pick any number of independent options.

## When to use

- For several independent choices.
- To accept terms.
- A parent checkbox can show a mixed (indeterminate) state.

## When not to use

- For a single choice among several: use [radio buttons](radio.md).
- For something that applies right away: use a [switch](switch.md).

## Variants and props

| Class or state | What it does |
|---|---|
| `aipim-checkbox` | The label that wraps the input, the box and the text. The whole row is the click target. |
| `aipim-checkbox__input` | The real input. It stays in the page, hidden visually. |
| `aipim-checkbox__box` | The drawn box. Put `aria-hidden="true"` on it. |
| `aipim-checkbox__label` | The text. |
| `:checked` | Checked: a check mark. |
| `input.indeterminate = true` | Indeterminate: a dash. It is set in code, there is no HTML attribute. |
| `aipim-choice-group` | A fieldset for a group. `aipim-choice-group--horizontal` lays it out in a row. Its legend is `aipim-choice-group__legend`. |

The label is part of the control: clicking it toggles the box.

## States

Default, hover, focus and disabled, for unchecked, checked and indeterminate. Hover darkens the border (and the fill when checked). Focus is a 3px ring, 3px away from the box. Disabled uses `opacity/disabled` on the box and the label.

## Tokens used

| Applies to | State | Token | Light | Dark |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Box fill | Unchecked | `bg/surface` | #FDF9F6 | #302A25 |
| Box border | Unchecked | `border/strong` | #837A73 | #A39992 |
| Box border | Unchecked, hover | `text/secondary` | #4A423C | #ECE5DF |
| Box fill and border | Checked, indeterminate | `action/primary/bg` | #B43000 | #FF9275 |
| Box fill and border | Checked, indeterminate, hover | `action/primary/hover` | #892402 | #FEBBA9 |
| Check mark | Checked, indeterminate | `action/primary/text` | #FDF9F6 | #1A1511 |
| Label | All | `text/primary` | #1A1511 | #FDF9F6 |
| Focus ring | Focus | `focus/ring` | #0364C2 | #AED1FE |
| Whole checkbox | Disabled | `opacity/disabled` | 40% | 40% |

| Measure | Token | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Box size | `size/icon-md` | 20 |
| Check mark size | `size/icon-sm` | 16 |
| Check mark stroke | No token | 2 |
| Gap between box and label | `space/12` | 12 |
| Row height | `Aipim/body` line height | 24 |
| Corner radius | `radius/sm` | 4 |
| Border width | `border/medium` | 2 |
| Label type | `Aipim/body` | 16/24 Regular |

The row is 24px tall: it meets the 24px minimum target and is below the 44px comfortable one.

## Accessibility

- Use the native `input type="checkbox"` with a label.
- A group sits in a `fieldset` with a `legend`.
- The indeterminate state is set in code, with the `indeterminate` property.
- Space toggles the checkbox. Tab moves focus, and the ring is always visible.

## Code examples

```html
<fieldset class="aipim-choice-group">
  <legend class="aipim-choice-group__legend">Notifications</legend>
  <label class="aipim-checkbox">
    <input class="aipim-checkbox__input" type="checkbox" checked>
    <span class="aipim-checkbox__box" aria-hidden="true"></span>
    <span class="aipim-checkbox__label">Email</span>
  </label>
  <label class="aipim-checkbox">
    <input class="aipim-checkbox__input" type="checkbox">
    <span class="aipim-checkbox__box" aria-hidden="true"></span>
    <span class="aipim-checkbox__label">SMS</span>
  </label>
</fieldset>

<script>
  document.querySelector('#parent').indeterminate = true;
</script>
```

## Do and don't

- Do: independent choices, each can be on or off.
- Don't: one-of-many choices need radio buttons.


---

<!-- docs/en/components/icon-button.md · class aipim-icon-button · WCAG ["1.4.11 Non-text Contrast", "2.4.7 Focus Visible", "2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum)", "4.1.2 Name, Role, Value"] -->
# Icon button

A button that shows only an icon.

## When to use

- For a familiar action that needs no label, such as close, back or search.
- In top bars, toolbars and other places where space is short.
- Always with an accessible name, because the icon has no text.

## When not to use

- For the main action of a screen: use a [button](button.md) with a label.
- For an action people may not recognize from the icon alone: add a label.
- To go to another page: use a [link](link.md).

## Variants and props

| Class | What it does |
|---|---|
| `aipim-icon-button` | Medium: a 44px target with a 24px icon. The default. |
| `aipim-icon-button--sm` | Small: a 24px target with a 16px icon. Only where space is tight. |

One style: no fill, and the fill shows on hover. The icon is any line icon from the [icon set](../../../icons/).

Two other small buttons are not icon buttons on purpose: the Alert dismiss button (`aipim-dismiss`) sits on a tinted surface where a gray hover fill would look wrong, and the Tag remove button is round to follow the tag.

## States

Default, hover, focus and disabled. Pressed looks like hover.

- **Hover and pressed:** a `bg/sunken` fill.
- **Disabled:** the native `disabled` attribute (or `aria-disabled="true"` on a link). Opacity is `opacity/disabled` (40%).
- **Focus:** a 3px ring in `focus/ring`, 3px away (`focus/offset`). It shows for keyboard focus only (`:focus-visible`).

## Tokens used

| Applies to | State | Token | Light | Dark |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Icon | All | `text/primary` | #1A1511 | #FDF9F6 |
| Container fill | Hover and pressed | `bg/sunken` | #ECE5DF | #0E0A07 |
| Focus ring | Focus | `focus/ring` | #0364C2 | #AED1FE |
| Whole button | Disabled | `opacity/disabled` | 40% | 40% |

| Measure | Token | Small | Medium |
|---|---|---|---|
| Size (width and height) | `size/touch-min`, `size/touch-comfortable` | 24 | 44 |
| Icon size | `size/icon-sm`, `size/icon-lg` | 16 | 24 |
| Padding, all sides | (size − icon) ÷ 2, no token | 4 | 10 |
| Corner radius | `radius/sm`, `radius/md` | 4 | 8 |
| Focus ring width | `border/thick` | 3 | 3 |
| Focus ring offset | `focus/offset` | 3 | 3 |

Small meets the 24px minimum (`size/touch-min`) and is below the 44px comfortable target (`size/touch-comfortable`). Medium meets both. Use Medium wherever touch is the main input.

## Accessibility

- Use the native `button` element (or `a` when it goes somewhere). Enter and Space activate a button.
- Always give it an `aria-label` that names the action, such as "Close". The icon is decorative: `aria-hidden="true"`.
- A toggle needs `aria-pressed`.
- Tab moves focus, and the ring is always visible. A disabled button leaves the tab order.

## Code examples

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="aipim.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="aipim-components.css">

<button class="aipim-icon-button" type="button" aria-label="Close">
  <svg class="aipim-icon" aria-hidden="true"><use href="icons/sprite.svg#aipim-close"></use></svg>
</button>

<!-- Small -->
<button class="aipim-icon-button aipim-icon-button--sm" type="button" aria-label="Dismiss">
  <svg class="aipim-icon" aria-hidden="true"><use href="icons/sprite.svg#aipim-close"></use></svg>
</button>
```

## Do and don't

- Do: use a familiar icon and name it with an `aria-label` (Close).
- Don't: use unclear icons with no label. They are guesswork: add a visible label.


---

<!-- docs/en/components/link.md · class aipim-link · WCAG ["1.4.1 Use of Color", "1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum)", "2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context)", "2.4.7 Focus Visible"] -->
# Link

Takes the reader to another page or section.

## When to use

- To go to another page or section.
- Inside running text.
- For a short action that only navigates.

## When not to use

- To run an action, such as saving: use a [button](button.md).
- For the main action of a screen: use a primary button.

## Variants and props

| Class | What it does |
|---|---|
| `aipim-link` | Inline. Inherits the type of the surrounding text. |
| `aipim-link aipim-link--standalone` | Stands on its own, in the label style (16/20 Bold), with an optional icon after the text. |

The underline is always on, so the link never depends on color alone. An optional 16px icon (`external-link`) can follow the text in a standalone link.

## States

Default, hover, focus and visited. Hover darkens the color (lightens it in dark theme). Visited uses `link/visited`. Focus is a 3px ring, 3px away, with rounded corners (`radius/sm`).

## Tokens used

| Applies to | State | Token | Light | Dark |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Label, underline and icon | Default | `link` | #014B95 | #8CBEFE |
| Label, underline and icon | Hover, pressed | `link/hover` | #00346B | #AED1FE |
| Label, underline and icon | Visited | `link/visited` | #892402 | #FEBBA9 |
| Focus ring | Focus | `focus/ring` | #0364C2 | #AED1FE |

| Measure | Token | Inline | Standalone |
|---|---|---|---|
| Type | `Aipim/body`, `Aipim/label` | 16/24 Regular | 16/20 Bold |
| Icon size | `size/icon-sm` | none | 16 |
| Gap between label and icon | `space/4` | none | 4 |
| Focus ring corner radius | `radius/sm` | 4 | 4 |
| Focus ring width and offset | `border/thick`, `focus/offset` | 3 and 3 | 3 and 3 |

A standalone link is 20px tall, which is below the 24px minimum target (`size/touch-min`). Give it space around it, or put it in a larger row, where touch matters.

## Accessibility

- Use the native `a` element with an `href`.
- Enter activates it. Tab moves focus, and the ring is always visible.
- A link that opens a new tab says so in its text.
- Link text makes sense out of context: avoid "click here".

## Code examples

```html
<p>Read the <a class="aipim-link" href="/accessibility">accessibility notes</a> before you ship.</p>

<a class="aipim-link aipim-link--standalone" href="https://example.com">
  External link
  <svg class="aipim-icon" aria-hidden="true"><use href="icons/sprite.svg#aipim-external-link"></use></svg>
</a>
```

## Do and don't

- Do: link text says where it goes ("Read the accessibility notes").
- Don't: "Click here" means nothing out of context.


---

<!-- docs/en/components/radio.md · class aipim-radio · WCAG ["1.3.1 Info and Relationships", "1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum)", "1.4.11 Non-text Contrast", "2.4.7 Focus Visible", "2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum)", "4.1.2 Name, Role, Value"] -->
# Radio

Lets a person pick one option from a short list.

## When to use

- For one choice among 2 to 6 visible options.
- When people should compare the options side by side.

## When not to use

- More than 6 options: use a select.
- For yes or no: use a [checkbox](checkbox.md) or a [switch](switch.md).

## Variants and props

| Class or state | What it does |
|---|---|
| `aipim-radio` | The label that wraps the input, the circle and the text. The whole row is the click target. |
| `aipim-radio__input` | The real input. All options of a group share one `name`. |
| `aipim-radio__circle` | The drawn circle. Put `aria-hidden="true"` on it. |
| `aipim-radio__label` | The text. |
| `:checked` | Selected: a 10px dot. |
| `aipim-choice-group` | A fieldset for the group (from `checkbox.css`). `aipim-choice-group--horizontal` lays it out in a row. |

Groups can be vertical or horizontal.

## States

Default, hover, focus and disabled, for off and on. Hover darkens the border (and the border and dot when selected). Focus is a 3px ring, 3px away from the circle. Disabled uses `opacity/disabled`.

## Tokens used

| Applies to | State | Token | Light | Dark |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Circle fill | All | `bg/surface` | #FDF9F6 | #302A25 |
| Circle border | Off | `border/strong` | #837A73 | #A39992 |
| Circle border | Off, hover | `text/secondary` | #4A423C | #ECE5DF |
| Circle border and dot | On | `action/primary/bg` | #B43000 | #FF9275 |
| Circle border and dot | On, hover | `action/primary/hover` | #892402 | #FEBBA9 |
| Label | All | `text/primary` | #1A1511 | #FDF9F6 |
| Focus ring | Focus | `focus/ring` | #0364C2 | #AED1FE |
| Whole radio | Disabled | `opacity/disabled` | 40% | 40% |

| Measure | Token | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Circle size | `size/icon-md` | 20 |
| Dot size | no token, half the circle | 10 |
| Gap between circle and label | `space/12` | 12 |
| Row height | `Aipim/body` line height | 24 |
| Corner radius | `radius/full` | fully round |
| Border width | `border/medium` | 2 |
| Label type | `Aipim/body` | 16/24 Regular |

The row is 24px tall: it meets the 24px minimum target and is below the 44px comfortable one.

## Accessibility

- Use the native `input type="radio"` sharing one `name`.
- A group sits in a `fieldset` with a `legend`, or `role="radiogroup"`.
- Preselect an option when there is a sensible default.
- Arrow keys move the choice inside the group. Tab enters and leaves the group, not each option. Space selects the focused option.

## Code examples

```html
<fieldset class="aipim-choice-group">
  <legend class="aipim-choice-group__legend">Plan</legend>
  <label class="aipim-radio">
    <input class="aipim-radio__input" type="radio" name="plan" checked>
    <span class="aipim-radio__circle" aria-hidden="true"></span>
    <span class="aipim-radio__label">Monthly</span>
  </label>
  <label class="aipim-radio">
    <input class="aipim-radio__input" type="radio" name="plan">
    <span class="aipim-radio__circle" aria-hidden="true"></span>
    <span class="aipim-radio__label">Yearly</span>
  </label>
</fieldset>
```

## Do and don't

- Do: a group with a legend, one option selected.
- Don't: a single radio cannot be turned off.


---

<!-- docs/en/components/switch.md · class aipim-switch · WCAG ["1.4.1 Use of Color", "1.4.11 Non-text Contrast", "2.4.7 Focus Visible", "2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum)", "4.1.2 Name, Role, Value"] -->
# Switch

Turns a setting on or off, and the change applies right away.

## When to use

- For a setting that takes effect immediately.
- For on or off preferences, such as notifications.

## When not to use

- When the choice needs a submit button: use a [checkbox](checkbox.md).
- For choosing between two named options: use [radio buttons](radio.md).

## Variants and props

| Class or state | What it does |
|---|---|
| `aipim-switch` | The label that wraps the input, the track and the text. The whole row is the click target. |
| `aipim-switch__input` | The real input: `type="checkbox"` with `role="switch"`. |
| `aipim-switch__track` | The drawn track and knob. Put `aria-hidden="true"` on it. |
| `aipim-switch__label` | The text, to the right of the track. |
| `:checked` | On: the track takes the primary color and the knob slides right. |

## States

Default, hover, focus and disabled, for off and on. Hover darkens the track. Focus is a 3px ring, 3px away from the track. Disabled uses `opacity/disabled`. The knob moves with `duration/fast` and `ease/standard`, and does not move with reduced motion.

## Tokens used

| Applies to | State | Token | Light | Dark |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Track | Off | `border/strong` | #837A73 | #A39992 |
| Track | Off, hover | `text/muted` | #665D56 | #DAD1CA |
| Track | On | `action/primary/bg` | #B43000 | #FF9275 |
| Track | On, hover | `action/primary/hover` | #892402 | #FEBBA9 |
| Knob | Off | `bg/surface` | #FDF9F6 | #302A25 |
| Knob | On | `action/primary/text` | #FDF9F6 | #1A1511 |
| Label | All | `text/primary` | #1A1511 | #FDF9F6 |
| Focus ring | Focus | `focus/ring` | #0364C2 | #AED1FE |
| Whole switch | Disabled | `opacity/disabled` | 40% | 40% |

| Measure | Token | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Track width | `size/touch-comfortable` | 44 |
| Track height | `size/touch-min` | 24 |
| Knob size | `size/icon-sm` | 16 |
| Space between track edge and knob | `space/4` | 4 |
| Gap between track and label | `space/12` | 12 |
| Track corner radius | `radius/full` | fully round |
| Label type | `Aipim/body` | 16/24 Regular |

The track is 24px tall: it meets the 24px minimum target and is below the 44px comfortable one.

## Accessibility

- Use `role="switch"` on a checkbox input (it carries `aria-checked` for you), or a button with `role="switch"` and `aria-checked`.
- The label names what it controls, such as "Notifications", not the state.
- The state also shows in the knob position, not only in color.
- Space toggles the switch. Tab moves focus, and the ring is always visible.

## Code examples

```html
<label class="aipim-switch">
  <input class="aipim-switch__input" type="checkbox" role="switch" checked>
  <span class="aipim-switch__track" aria-hidden="true"></span>
  <span class="aipim-switch__label">Notifications</span>
</label>
```

## Do and don't

- Do: the label names the setting ("Notifications").
- Don't: the label should not describe the action or state ("Turn notifications on").


---

<!-- docs/en/components/tag.md · class aipim-tag · WCAG ["1.4.1 Use of Color", "1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum)", "2.4.7 Focus Visible", "2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum)", "4.1.2 Name, Role, Value"] -->
# Tag

A short label for a category, a technology or a status.

## When to use

- For a short label: a category, a technology or a status.
- To show attributes of an item.
- Removable, when people choose the tags themselves.

## When not to use

- For actions: use a [button](button.md).
- For long text or whole sentences.
- For a status that needs attention: use an [alert](alert.md).

## Variants and props

| Class | What it does |
|---|---|
| `aipim-tag` | Outline. A 1px border in `border/strong`. |
| `aipim-tag--accent` | Filled with the accent color, no border. |
| `aipim-tag--inverse` | For a dark or colored surface, such as a masthead. No fill. Label, icon and border follow the text color of the surface. |
| `aipim-tag--link` | A tag that goes somewhere: use an `a`. Label in the link color, underlined. It has no remove button. |
| `aipim-tag > .aipim-icon` | Optional 16px icon before the label. |
| `aipim-tag__remove` | Optional remove button, only for tags the user can take away. |

## States

A tag that is not removable or a link has no states and is not focusable. The remove button has hover (fill) and focus (3px ring, 3px away). A link tag has hover (the label changes to `link/hover`), visited (`link/visited`) and focus (a 3px ring around the whole tag, 3px away).

## Tokens used

| Applies to | State | Token | Light | Dark |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Outline border | All | `border/strong` | #837A73 | #A39992 |
| Outline label, icon and remove icon | All | `text/primary` | #1A1511 | #FDF9F6 |
| Outline remove button fill | Remove hover | `bg/sunken` | #ECE5DF | #0E0A07 |
| Accent fill | All | `accent/bg` | #FFD337 | #FFD337 |
| Accent label | All | `accent/text` | #1A1511 | #1A1511 |
| Accent remove button fill | Remove hover | `bg/surface` | #FDF9F6 | #302A25 |
| Link label and icon | Default | `link` | #014B95 | #8CBEFE |
| Link label | Hover | `link/hover` | #00346B | #AED1FE |
| Link label | Visited | `link/visited` | #892402 | #FEBBA9 |
| Link border | All | `border/strong` | #837A73 | #A39992 |
| Inverse label, icon and remove icon | All | Text color of the surface | Inherited | Inherited |
| Inverse border | All | Text color of the surface at 60% | Inherited | Inherited |
| Inverse remove button fill | Remove hover | Text color of the surface at 16% | Inherited | Inherited |
| Focus ring | Focus | `focus/ring` | #0364C2 | #AED1FE |

| Measure | Token | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Vertical padding | `space/4` | 4 |
| Horizontal padding | `space/12` | 12 |
| Gap between items | `space/8` | 8 |
| Height without remove button | Label line height plus padding | 29 |
| Height with remove button | Remove button plus padding | 32 |
| Icon size | `size/icon-sm` | 16 |
| Remove button size | `size/touch-min` | 24 |
| Corner radius | `radius/full` | Fully round |
| Outline border width | `border/thin` | 1 |
| Label type | `Aipim/body-sm` | 14/21 Regular |

Sizes are measured from the outer edge. In code the border is always 1px (transparent on the accent tag) and it comes out of the padding, so both styles are the same size.

The remove button is 24px: it meets `size/touch-min` and is below `size/touch-comfortable` (44).

## Accessibility

- The text is always visible, never an icon alone.
- A remove button needs an `aria-label` that names the tag, such as "Remove design". Enter and Space remove the tag; `aipim.js` then moves focus to the next focusable element.
- A group of tags is a list (`ul` and `li`), so screen readers announce how many there are.
- The accent label meets 4.5:1 contrast on the accent fill in both themes.
- An inverse tag has no colors of its own: check that the text color of the surface meets 4.5:1 against the surface. In the Figma file the Inverse style uses the Dark mode of the Semantic collection, so it belongs on dark surfaces.
- A link tag is an `a` with a real `href`. The underline is always on, so the link is not shown by color alone. Do not put a remove button inside it.

## Code examples

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="aipim.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="aipim-components.css">

<ul role="list" style="display:flex;gap:8px;list-style:none;padding:0">
  <li><span class="aipim-tag"><span>Design</span></span></li>
  <li>
    <span class="aipim-tag aipim-tag--accent">
      <span>Design</span>
      <button class="aipim-tag__remove" type="button" aria-label="Remove design" data-aipim-dismiss>
        <svg class="aipim-icon" aria-hidden="true"><use href="icons/sprite.svg#aipim-close"></use></svg>
      </button>
    </span>
  </li>
</ul>

<!-- Inverse, on a dark surface -->
<div data-theme="dark" style="background:var(--aipim-bg-canvas);color:var(--aipim-text-primary);padding:16px">
  <span class="aipim-tag aipim-tag--inverse"><span>Design</span></span>
</div>

<!-- Link -->
<a class="aipim-tag aipim-tag--link" href="/tags/design"><span>Design</span></a>
```

## Do and don't

- Do: a short label of one or two words ("Design").
- Don't: use a sentence as a tag. Use plain text.


---

<!-- docs/en/components/accordion.md · class aipim-accordion · WCAG ["1.3.1 Info and Relationships", "1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum)", "2.4.7 Focus Visible", "2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum)", "4.1.2 Name, Role, Value"] -->
# Accordion

A title that opens a panel of text. It hides what most people do not need to read and lets the rest find it in one line: frequent questions, rules, the details of an order.

## When to use

- Frequent questions and help texts, where each person wants to read one or two items.
- The details of an order or of a rule, which matter only to whoever opens them.

## When not to use

- Content that everyone needs to read to decide: leave it in view.
- To switch between sections of the same weight: use [tabs](tabs.md).
- Inside another accordion: one level only.

## Decision: a native element, no script

The item is a `details` with a `summary`. The browser opens and closes it, and the keyboard and the screen reader come for free. Aipim only styles it. To open one at a time, give the `details` of the group the same `name`; without it, each one opens on its own.

## Decision: the whole header is the target

The row of the title opens and closes the item, not only the chevron, and it is at least 44px high. The chevron points at what will happen (down opens, up closes), and the browser already tells a screen reader whether the item is open or closed.

## Variants and props

| Class or attribute | What it does |
|---|---|
| `aipim-accordion` on `details` | One item. It draws the divider under it, so items one after the other form the accordion. |
| `aipim-accordion__header` on `summary` | The header: the title and the chevron. |
| `aipim-accordion__title` | The title. |
| `aipim-accordion__chevron` | The chevron icon (`chevron-down`), `aria-hidden="true"`. It turns up when the item is open. |
| `aipim-accordion__panel` | The panel with the text, shown when the item is open. |
| `open` on the `details` | Starts the item open. |
| `name` on the `details` | The same value in a group: only one item stays open. |

## States

| State | What changes |
|---|---|
| Closed, open | The panel shows only when open, and the chevron turns up. |
| Hover | The header fills with `bg/sunken`. |
| Focus | A 3px ring drawn around the whole item, inside it. |

There is no disabled state. A `details` has none of its own, and an item that cannot be opened should not be on the page. If it must be there, say why in the title or in the text next to it.

## Tokens used

| Applies to | State | Token | Light | Dark |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Title | All | `text/primary` | #1A1511 | #FDF9F6 |
| Panel and chevron | All | `text/secondary` | #4A423C | #ECE5DF |
| Header | Hover | `bg/sunken` | #ECE5DF | #0E0A07 |
| Divider | All | `border/subtle` | #DAD1CA | #4A423C |
| Focus ring | Focus | `focus/ring` | #0364C2 | #AED1FE |

| Measure | Token | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Minimum height of the header | `size/touch-comfortable` | 44 |
| Horizontal padding | `space/16` | 16 |
| Vertical padding of the header | `space/12` | 12 |
| Space between title and chevron | `space/12` | 12 |
| Chevron | `size/icon-md` | 20 |
| Padding under the panel | `space/16` | 16 |
| Divider | `border/thin` | 1, over the bottom edge, no extra height |
| Focus ring | `border/thick` | 3, inside the item |

## Accessibility

- It is `details` and `summary`: the browser says "collapsed" or "expanded" by itself.
- Tab and Shift+Tab go from header to header. An open panel is not a stop, only what is inside it.
- Enter and Space open or close the item in focus.
- The same `name` on the `details` of a group makes them open one at a time.
- The chevron is `aria-hidden="true"`.
- The panel is the text inside the `details`, read when it is open.

## Code examples

```html
<details class="aipim-accordion" name="pix" open>
  <summary class="aipim-accordion__header">
    <span class="aipim-accordion__title">When does Pix arrive?</span>
    <svg class="aipim-icon aipim-accordion__chevron" aria-hidden="true"><use href="icons/sprite.svg#aipim-chevron-down"></use></svg>
  </summary>
  <div class="aipim-accordion__panel">
    <p>Pix arrives in seconds, at any hour, including holidays.</p>
  </div>
</details>
<details class="aipim-accordion" name="pix">
  <summary class="aipim-accordion__header">
    <span class="aipim-accordion__title">Can I cancel a scheduled Pix?</span>
    <svg class="aipim-icon aipim-accordion__chevron" aria-hidden="true"><use href="icons/sprite.svg#aipim-chevron-down"></use></svg>
  </summary>
  <div class="aipim-accordion__panel">
    <p>Open the schedule in the app and choose cancel.</p>
  </div>
</details>
```

## Do and don't

- Do: short titles, the question or the subject, that fit on one line.
- Don't: titles that are whole sentences, where the row becomes a paragraph and cannot be read at a glance.

<!-- docs/en/components/alert.md · class aipim-alert · WCAG ["1.4.1 Use of Color", "1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum)", "2.4.7 Focus Visible", "2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum)", "4.1.2 Name, Role, Value", "4.1.3 Status Messages"] -->
# Alert

An important message that stays visible on the page.

## When to use

- For an important message that must stay visible on the page.
- For form-level errors, warnings and notices about the current state.
- With a title when the message needs a heading.

## When not to use

- For a passing confirmation, such as "Saved": use a [toast](toast.md).
- For an error on a single field: use the helper text of the [text field](text-field.md).

## Variants and props

| Class | What it does |
|---|---|
| `aipim-alert` | Info. The default type. |
| `aipim-alert--success` / `--warning` / `--error` | The other three types. |
| `aipim-alert__icon` | The type icon. Required, so color is never the only cue. |
| `aipim-alert__content` | Wraps the title and the message. |
| `aipim-alert__title` | Optional short summary in `Aipim/label`. |
| `aipim-alert__message` | What happened and what to do next. |
| `aipim-dismiss` | Optional dismiss button. It is not an [icon button](icon-button.md) on purpose: the alert surface is tinted, so a gray hover fill would look wrong. |

## States

An alert has no hover or pressed state. The dismiss button shows the focus ring (3px, `focus/ring`, 3px away) for keyboard focus only.

## Tokens used

| Applies to | Type | Token | Light | Dark |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Surface fill | Info | `info/bg` | #E4F0FF | #00346B |
| Border and type icon | Info | `info/icon` | #047DF1 | #8CBEFE |
| Title, message and dismiss icon | Info | `info/text` | #014B95 | #CEE3FF |
| Surface fill | Success | `success/bg` | #E0F5E6 | #014122 |
| Border and type icon | Success | `success/icon` | #007A44 | #C4EDD1 |
| Title, message and dismiss icon | Success | `success/text` | #025D33 | #C4EDD1 |
| Surface fill | Warning | `warning/bg` | #F6EED5 | #423400 |
| Border and type icon | Warning | `warning/icon` | #5E4B03 | #FFD337 |
| Title, message and dismiss icon | Warning | `warning/text` | #423400 | #F1E1B1 |
| Surface fill | Error | `error/bg` | #FEE8EC | #66022B |
| Border and type icon | Error | `error/icon` | #DE316D | #FF5387 |
| Title, message and dismiss icon | Error | `error/text` | #8F083F | #FFD5DC |

| Measure | Token | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Padding, all sides | `space-role/inset-md` | 16 |
| Gap between icon and text | `space/12` | 12 |
| Gap between title and message | `space/4` | 4 |
| Type icon size | `size/icon-md` | 20 |
| Dismiss button size | `size/touch-min` | 24 |
| Dismiss icon size | `size/icon-sm` | 16 |
| Dismiss button corner radius | `radius/sm` | 4 |
| Corner radius | `radius/md` | 8 |
| Border width | `border/thin` | 1 |
| Title type | `Aipim/label` | 16/20 Bold |
| Message type | `Aipim/body` | 16/24 Regular |

Sizes are measured from the outer edge: the 1px border comes out of the padding in code. With a title and a dismiss button the alert is 80px high, with a message only 56px.

The dismiss button is 24px, so it meets the 24px minimum (`size/touch-min`) and is below the 44px comfortable target (`size/touch-comfortable`).

## Accessibility

- `role="alert"` for errors and `role="status"` for information, warnings and successes. Put the role on the alert when it is added to the page, so screen readers announce it.
- Icon plus text, never color alone. The type icon is decorative: `aria-hidden="true"`.
- The dismiss button needs an accessible name, such as "Dismiss". Enter and Space activate it.
- After dismissing, move focus to a sensible place, such as the next element. `aipim.js` does this for `data-aipim-dismiss` buttons.
- The text colors have at least 4.5:1 contrast on their surface in both themes (WCAG 1.4.3).

## Code examples

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="aipim.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="aipim-components.css">

<div class="aipim-alert aipim-alert--error" role="alert">
  <svg class="aipim-icon aipim-alert__icon" aria-hidden="true"><use href="icons/sprite.svg#aipim-error"></use></svg>
  <div class="aipim-alert__content">
    <p class="aipim-alert__title">Payment failed</p>
    <p class="aipim-alert__message">Check your card details and try again.</p>
  </div>
  <button class="aipim-dismiss" type="button" aria-label="Dismiss" data-aipim-dismiss>
    <svg class="aipim-icon" aria-hidden="true"><use href="icons/sprite.svg#aipim-close"></use></svg>
  </button>
</div>
```

`data-aipim-dismiss` needs the optional `aipim.js`. Without it, remove the alert in your own handler.

## Do and don't

- Do: say what happened and what to do next ("Check your card details and try again").
- Don't: write a vague message ("Something went wrong"). It gives no way forward.

<!-- docs/en/components/brazilian-field.md · class aipim-field · WCAG ["1.3.1 Info and Relationships", "1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose", "3.3.1 Error Identification", "3.3.2 Labels or Instructions", "3.3.3 Error Suggestion", "4.1.2 Name, Role, Value"] -->
# Brazilian field

A text field for Brazilian data (CPF, CNPJ, CEP, phone, date and reais), with its mask and its check.

## When to use

- For the documents and formats every Brazilian form asks for: CPF, CNPJ, CEP, a phone with area code, a date as dd/mm/aaaa and an amount in reais.
- When the person types the value. A value picked from a list is a select.

## When not to use

- For a phone outside Brazil: use a [text field](text-field.md) with `type="tel"`.
- For a date picked on a calendar: a date picker (not in this version).
- For any other format. The six formats are the ones with a Brazilian rule behind them; a generic mask is not part of Aipim.

## How it works

It is a [text field](text-field.md) with `data-aipim-format` on the input. The look, the sizes, the states and the tokens are the ones of the text field. What changes comes from `components/web/aipim.js`:

- **While you type**, the mask goes in (dots, dashes, slash, parentheses) and the caret stays after the character you typed. Pasting works with or without the mask.
- **Backspace on a dot or a dash** deletes the digit before it. Without this, the mask would put the dot back and the caret would not move.
- **When you leave the field**, the value is checked. An error sets `aria-invalid="true"` and writes the message in the helper text.
- **As soon as the value is valid again**, the error goes away and the helper text comes back. The error never shows up while the person is still typing.

Without the script the field is a plain text field: the person can type the value with or without the mask. Check the value on the server in any case.

| Format | `data-aipim-format` | Mask | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|
| CPF | `cpf` | 000.000.000-00 | 11 digits, both check digits, not all the same digit |
| CNPJ | `cnpj` | AA.AAA.AAA/AAAA-00 (A is a letter or a digit) | 14 characters, letters only in the first 12, both check digits |
| CEP | `cep` | 00000-000 | 8 digits |
| Phone | `phone` | (00) 00000-0000 or (00) 0000-0000 | an area code that exists; a mobile number has 11 digits and starts with 9, a landline has 10 and starts with 2 to 5 |
| Date | `date` | dd/mm/aaaa | a date that exists, leap years included |
| Reais | `money` | R$ 1.234,56 | nothing: any amount is valid. Leaving the field writes the two decimals |

## Decision: the mask while typing, the check when leaving

A field that turns red at the first digit tells off the person for something they have not finished. A field that only formats when you leave it hides the format while you type, and the person counts digits on the screen. The mask while typing shows how much is left; the check when leaving says what is wrong only once there is something to say.

## Decision: a CNPJ with letters

Since July 2026 the Receita Federal gives out CNPJs with letters in the first 12 characters (Instrução Normativa RFB 2.229/2024). The two check digits stay numbers. So the CNPJ field has no `inputmode="numeric"`: a numeric keyboard would block the letters. Letters become capitals as you type, and the old CNPJs, all digits, still work.

## Decision: a typed date, not `type="date"`

The native date input shows the order of the browser's language, not the page's: a Brazilian on a computer in English sees mm/dd/yyyy. And for a date of birth, eight digits are faster than a calendar that opens on today. The date field is a text field with the dd/mm/aaaa mask.

## Variants and props

| Attribute | What it does |
|---|---|
| `data-aipim-format` | The format: `cpf`, `cnpj`, `cep`, `phone`, `date` or `money`. |
| `data-aipim-error-incomplete`, `data-aipim-error-invalid` | Your own error messages, instead of the ones in the script. |
| `data-aipim-help` on the helper's `span` | The helper text to bring back when an error rendered on the server is fixed. |

Put these on the input too, for the right keyboard on phones and for autofill:

| Format | Attributes |
|---|---|
| CPF | `inputmode="numeric"` |
| CNPJ | `autocapitalize="characters"`, `spellcheck="false"` |
| CEP | `inputmode="numeric"`, `autocomplete="postal-code"` |
| Phone | `type="tel"`, `autocomplete="tel-national"` |
| Date | `inputmode="numeric"`; for a date of birth, `autocomplete="bday"` |
| Reais | `inputmode="decimal"` |

Do not set `maxlength`: a pasted value with its mask or with +55 is longer than the value, and the script cuts the extra characters itself.

The messages are in Brazilian Portuguese when the nearest `lang` starts with `pt`, and in English otherwise.

## In code: `Aipim.br`

The same rules as plain functions, for a React or Vue app that controls its own value, and for the server. In a browser the script puts them on `Aipim.br`. Where there is no page, import the same three from the module: it touches no DOM, so it runs in Node, in a route handler and in a test.

```js
import { format, check, clean } from 'aipim-ds/br.js';

check('cpf', '390.533.447-05');  // ''
clean('date', '20/11/2026');     // '2026-11-20'
```


| Function | Returns |
|---|---|
| `Aipim.br.format(type, value, done)` | The value with its mask. `done` adds the two decimals of an amount. |
| `Aipim.br.check(type, value)` | `''` when valid or empty, `'incomplete'` or `'invalid'`. |
| `Aipim.br.clean(type, value)` | The value to store: the digits (a CNPJ in capitals), a date as `yyyy-mm-dd`, an amount as `1234.56`. `''` when the value is not valid. |

## Accessibility

- Everything in the [text field](text-field.md): a label above the field, helper and error text linked with `aria-describedby`, an error with an icon and text.
- The helper text says the format before anyone gets it wrong ("Type only the numbers", "With the area code").
- The error says what is wrong and what to check ("A CPF has 11 digits. Check if one is missing."), in line with 3.3.3 Error Suggestion.
- The message is not announced while focus is elsewhere. Screen readers read it when the person comes back to the field. When a form is sent with errors, move focus to the first invalid field.
- The `autocomplete` values let browsers fill the CEP, the phone and the date of birth (1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose).

## Code examples

```html
<div class="aipim-field">
  <label class="aipim-field__label" for="cpf">CPF</label>
  <input class="aipim-field__control" id="cpf" name="cpf" type="text" inputmode="numeric" data-aipim-format="cpf" aria-describedby="cpf-help">
  <p class="aipim-field__helper" aria-live="polite" id="cpf-help">
    <svg class="aipim-icon aipim-field__icon" aria-hidden="true"><use href="icons/sprite.svg#aipim-error"></use></svg>
    <span>Type only the numbers</span>
  </p>
</div>
```

```js
// React: format in onChange, check in onBlur.
const [cpf, setCpf] = useState('');
<input value={cpf} onChange={(e) => setCpf(Aipim.br.format('cpf', e.target.value))}
  onBlur={() => setError(Aipim.br.check('cpf', cpf))} />
```

## Do and don't

- Do: the helper text says the format, and the mask shows how much is left.
- Don't: a placeholder with the mask as the only hint, gone at the first digit.

<!-- docs/en/components/card.md · class aipim-card · WCAG ["1.1.1 Non-text Content", "1.3.1 Info and Relationships", "2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context)", "2.4.7 Focus Visible"] -->
# Card

Groups related content on one surface. It can be a single link.

## When to use

- To group related content on one surface.
- A clickable card when the whole block leads to one place.
- A card with an image to give the content a visual anchor.

## When not to use

- For everything: not every block needs a card.
- Cards inside cards: use spacing instead.
- Several links or buttons that compete: pick one clear action.

## Variants and props

| Class | What it does |
|---|---|
| `aipim-card` | A static card. |
| `aipim-card--primary`, `--secondary`, `--tertiary`, `--success` | Tone. Fills the card with a vivid tint (urucum, azulejo blue, cajá yellow, leaf green) and no visible border. Without one, the card is a surface. Combines with `--interactive`. |
| `aipim-card--interactive` | The whole card leads to one place. It gets a hover shadow and a focus ring on the card. |
| `aipim-card__media` | Optional image area across the top, 160px tall. Put an `img` inside, or an icon as a placeholder. |
| `aipim-card__body` | Holds the text parts. |
| `aipim-card__header` | Optional. One line with up to two extras around the title: a [badge](badge.md) before it and an eyebrow above it. They are vertically centered. |
| `aipim-card__heading` | Inside the header, holds the eyebrow and the title. It takes the free space and the title wraps, so the badge keeps its size. |
| `aipim-card__eyebrow` | Optional small label above the title, in `Aipim/overline`. A category, a step or a stage. |
| `aipim-card__title` | `Aipim/h4`. |
| `aipim-card__text` | A short description in `Aipim/body`. |
| `aipim-card__action` | A link-style label, such as Learn more. It is a label only: the card is the link. |
| `aipim-card__link` | The one link, inside the title. Its `::after` covers the card, so the card is a single focus stop. |

## States

- **Static:** no states.
- **Interactive:** hover shows the `raised` shadow. Focus shows a 3px ring around the whole card, 3px away (`focus/ring`, `focus/offset`), for keyboard focus only.

## Tokens used

| Applies to | State | Token | Light | Dark |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Surface fill | All | `bg/surface` | #FDF9F6 | #302A25 |
| Border | All | `border/subtle` | #DAD1CA | #4A423C |
| Media placeholder fill | All | `bg/sunken` | #ECE5DF | #0E0A07 |
| Media placeholder icon | All | `text/muted` | #665D56 | #DAD1CA |
| Title | All | `text/primary` | #1A1511 | #FDF9F6 |
| Text | All | `text/secondary` | #4A423C | #ECE5DF |
| Action label | Default | `link` | #014B95 | #8CBEFE |
| Eyebrow | All | `text/muted` | #665D56 | #DAD1CA |
| Eyebrow on a tone | All | `tint/text/muted` | #4A423C | #ECE5DF |
| Tone fill: primary, secondary, tertiary, success | All | `tint/primary`, `tint/secondary`, `tint/tertiary`, `tint/success` | #FEBBA9, #AED1FE, #FFD337, #A0DFB5 | #892402, #014B95, #5E4B03, #025D33 |
| Tone title and action label | All | `tint/text` | #1A1511 | #FDF9F6 |
| Tone text | All | `tint/text/muted` | #4A423C | #ECE5DF |
| Tone media placeholder fill | All | `tint/text` at 10% | #1A1511 at 10% | #FDF9F6 at 10% |
| Tone media placeholder icon | All | `tint/text/muted` | #4A423C | #ECE5DF |
| Focus ring | Focus | `focus/ring` | #0364C2 | #AED1FE |

| Measure | Token | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Padding, all sides | `space-role/inset-lg` | 24 |
| Gap between text parts | `space/12` | 12 |
| Gap between badge and text (header) | `space/16` | 16 |
| Gap between eyebrow and title | `space/4` | 4 |
| Media height | No token | 160 |
| Media icon size | `size/icon-lg` | 24 |
| Corner radius | `radius/xl` | 16 |
| Border width | `border/thin` | 1 |
| Title type | `Aipim/h4` | 24 SemiBold |
| Text type | `Aipim/body` | 16/24 Regular |
| Eyebrow type | `Aipim/overline` | 12/18 Bold, uppercase |
| Action label type | `Aipim/label` | 16/20 Bold, underlined |
| Shadow on hover (interactive) | `Aipim/elevation/raised` | 0 4 12 -2 at 12%, 0 2 4 -1 at 6% (light). 50% and 30% in dark. |

Sizes are measured from the outer edge: the 1px border comes out of the padding and the media height in code. The card fills the width of its container.

## Accessibility

- The title is a heading at the right level. Put the link inside the heading.
- The whole card is one link. Never nest buttons or links inside an interactive card.
- A clickable card is one focus stop, on the link in its title. Enter activates it.
- Images that only decorate have empty `alt` text.
- A badge in the header is decorative: `aria-hidden="true"`, and the title says what the card is. On a tone, use the filled badge, because the tint badge disappears on a tint.
- The eyebrow is a `p` before the heading, not a heading.
- A badge and an eyebrow work together: keep the title short, because it wraps when the badge takes its space.
- A card has a badge or no badge; there is no tag in the card. For a status, put the word in the text or use the tone.
- On a tone, the title meets AAA contrast and the text meets AA against the tint, in both themes (see the pairs in the color page). The action label follows the title color, not the link color, which is not checked against tints.
- A tone is decoration and emphasis, never the only way to tell cards apart: the title and text say what each card is.

## Code examples

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="aipim.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="aipim-components.css">

<!-- Static -->
<article class="aipim-card">
  <div class="aipim-card__body">
    <h3 class="aipim-card__title">Card title</h3>
    <p class="aipim-card__text">A short description of what is inside this card.</p>
  </div>
</article>

<!-- Interactive, with media -->
<article class="aipim-card aipim-card--interactive">
  <div class="aipim-card__media"><img src="cover.jpg" alt=""></div>
  <div class="aipim-card__body">
    <h3 class="aipim-card__title"><a class="aipim-card__link" href="/learn">Card title</a></h3>
    <p class="aipim-card__text">A short description of what is inside this card.</p>
    <span class="aipim-card__action">Learn more</span>
  </div>
</article>

<!-- Header with a badge and an eyebrow -->
<article class="aipim-card">
  <div class="aipim-card__body">
    <div class="aipim-card__header">
      <span class="aipim-badge aipim-badge--tint aipim-badge--square" aria-hidden="true">
        <svg class="aipim-icon" aria-hidden="true"><use href="icons/sprite.svg#aipim-info"></use></svg>
      </span>
      <div class="aipim-card__heading">
        <p class="aipim-card__eyebrow">Start</p>
        <h3 class="aipim-card__title">Card title</h3>
      </div>
    </div>
    <p class="aipim-card__text">A short description of what is inside this card.</p>
  </div>
</article>

<!-- Tone -->
<article class="aipim-card aipim-card--tertiary">
  <div class="aipim-card__body">
    <h3 class="aipim-card__title">Card title</h3>
    <p class="aipim-card__text">A short description of what is inside this card.</p>
  </div>
</article>
```

## Do and don't

- Do: one clear action for the whole card.
- Don't: put a card inside a card. It adds noise: use spacing instead.


---

<!-- docs/en/components/combobox.md · class aipim-combobox · WCAG ["1.3.1 Info and Relationships", "1.4.11 Non-text Contrast", "2.1.1 Keyboard", "2.4.7 Focus Visible", "3.3.1 Error Identification", "3.3.3 Error Suggestion", "4.1.2 Name, Role, Value", "4.1.3 Status Messages"] -->
# Combobox

A text field that filters a list of options while you type, for long lists such as the states of Brazil or the banks.

## When to use

- One choice from a long list the person knows by name: the state, the bank, the city.
- When typing two or three letters is faster than scrolling: "ba" finds Bahia, "sp" finds São Paulo.

## When not to use

- A short list: use a [select](select.md), or [radio buttons](radio.md) for five options or fewer.
- Free text with suggestions, where any value is accepted (a search box): this combobox only accepts one of its options.
- To pick more than one option: not in this version.

## How it works

The field is an `input` with `role="combobox"`, and the options are a `ul` with `role="listbox"` in a popup under it. `aipim.js` does the rest.

- **Typing** opens the list and keeps only the options that contain the text, without caring for accents or capitals: "sao" finds "São Paulo". The text also finds an option by its `data-value` when it is the whole value, so "sp" finds São Paulo.
- **Down** or **Up** on a closed list opens it with every option. **Alt+Down** only opens it.
- **Down** and **Up** move the option under the arrows, and wrap from the last to the first. Focus stays in the field and `aria-activedescendant` names that option, so a screen reader reads it.
- **Enter** or a **click** chooses the option: its name goes in the field and its `data-value` in the hidden input of the field, when there is one. The field fires `change`.
- **Escape** closes the list. With the list closed, Escape clears the field.
- **Tab** closes the list and moves on, without choosing.
- **Leaving the field** with a text that is not an option shows the error. A name typed in full, in any case and without accents, becomes that option.
- With no option left, the popup shows the empty message ("No state with that name").
- A screen reader hears the count of options found ("3 options") after a pause in the typing, from a `role="status"` the script adds.

Without the script the field is a plain text field and the list stays hidden: check the value on the server too.

## Decision: a list written in the page

The options are `li` elements in the HTML, not a JavaScript array. The page works the same with any framework, a reader of the code sees the options, and a server can render them. For a list too long for the page (the 5,570 Brazilian municipalities), filter on the server, write the options that came back and call `Aipim.init(field)`.

## Decision: chosen by hand, and only from the list

The list filters while you type but never picks for you. An option is chosen only by Enter, by a click, or by typing its whole name. Picking the first match on its own (automatic selection, in the ARIA pattern) surprises people who type fast and then press Tab. Accepting free text would send values the server does not know, so a text that is not an option is an error, with a message that says how to find it.

## Variants and props

| Class or attribute | What it does |
|---|---|
| `aipim-field aipim-combobox` | The wrapper. It uses the parts of the text field. |
| `aipim-field--lg` | Large field, 48px. Default is medium, 40px. The options stay 40px. |
| `role="combobox"`, `aria-autocomplete="list"`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls` on the input | The field. `aria-controls` names the listbox. Add `autocomplete="off"` so the browser's own suggestions do not cover the list. |
| `aipim-combobox__chevron` | The chevron after the field, `aria-hidden="true"`. It turns when the list is open. |
| `aipim-combobox__popup` with `hidden` | The box that opens under the field and scrolls. |
| `aipim-combobox__list`, `role="listbox"`, `aria-labelledby` | The list, named by the label of the field. |
| `aipim-combobox__option`, `role="option"`, `data-value` | One option. Its text is the name shown; `data-value` is the value sent (the UF, the bank code). |
| `aipim-combobox__empty` with `hidden` | The message for no option found. |
| `input type="hidden"` in the wrapper | Optional. Gets the `data-value` of the option chosen, for a form. |
| `data-aipim-error-invalid` on the input | Your own error message, in place of the default. |
| `--aipim-combobox-rows` | How many rows the popup shows before it scrolls. Default 6.5: the half row shows there is more. |

## States

The field has the states of the [text field](text-field.md): default, hover, focus, error and disabled. The list adds:

- **Option under the arrows:** a `bg/sunken` fill and a 3px bar in `action/primary/bg` on its start edge, so it is never shown by color alone.
- **Option under the pointer:** the `bg/sunken` fill.
- **Open:** the chevron points up.

## Tokens used

The field, the label and the helper text use the tokens of the [text field](text-field.md). The combobox adds:

| Applies to | State | Token | Light | Dark |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Chevron | All | `text/secondary` | #4A423C | #ECE5DF |
| Popup fill | Open | `bg/surface` | #FDF9F6 | #302A25 |
| Popup border | Open | `border/subtle` | #DAD1CA | #4A423C |
| Popup shadow | Open | `elevation/overlay` | | |
| Option text | All | `text/primary` | #1A1511 | #FDF9F6 |
| Option fill | Under the arrows, hover | `bg/sunken` | #ECE5DF | #0E0A07 |
| Option bar | Under the arrows | `action/primary/bg` | #B43000 | #FF9275 |
| Empty message | No option found | `text/secondary` | #4A423C | #ECE5DF |

| Measure | Token | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Option height | `size/control-md` | 40 |
| Option padding | `space/8`, `space-role/inset-sm` | 8, 12 |
| Gap between field and popup | `space/4` | 4 |
| Popup padding | `space/4` | 4 |
| Popup height before it scrolls | `size/control-md` × 6.5 + `space/8` | 268 |
| Bar of the option under the arrows | `border/thick` | 3 |
| Popup layer | `z/dropdown` | |
| Chevron turn | `duration/fast`, `easing/standard` | 100ms, 0ms with reduced motion |

## Accessibility

- It follows the [ARIA 1.2 combobox pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/combobox/), with list autocomplete and manual selection.
- A `label` associated with the input, and the listbox named by the same label (`aria-labelledby`).
- Focus never leaves the field while the list is open: the option under the arrows is named by `aria-activedescendant` and marked with `aria-selected="true"`.
- The count of options found is a status message (WCAG 4.1.3), read after a pause so it does not talk over the typing.
- An error shows an icon and text, never color alone, and says how to fix it.
- The popup scrolls inside its own box, so the page does not move under the arrows.
- Escape inside a [modal](modal.md) closes the list first; a second Escape clears the field, and only then does the next one close the modal.

### Screen readers

Checked by hand with each pair below. The browser checks cover the keyboard and the ARIA attributes; only a person can confirm what is read aloud.

| Screen reader | Browser | Status |
|---|---|---|
| VoiceOver (macOS) | Safari | To check |
| NVDA (Windows) | Firefox, Chrome | To check |
| TalkBack (Android) | Chrome | To check |

What to listen for: on focus, the label, "combo box" (or "text field, pop-up") and the helper text; after typing, the count of options; on Down, the name of the option; after Enter, the name chosen in the field; on leaving with a wrong text, the error message.

## Code examples

```html
<div class="aipim-field aipim-combobox">
  <label class="aipim-field__label" for="state" id="state-label">State</label>
  <input class="aipim-field__control" id="state" type="text" role="combobox" aria-autocomplete="list" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="state-list" aria-describedby="state-help" autocomplete="off">
  <input type="hidden" name="uf">
  <svg class="aipim-icon aipim-combobox__chevron" aria-hidden="true"><use href="icons/sprite.svg#aipim-chevron-down"></use></svg>
  <div class="aipim-combobox__popup" hidden>
    <ul class="aipim-combobox__list" id="state-list" role="listbox" aria-labelledby="state-label">
      <li class="aipim-combobox__option" role="option" id="state-ac" data-value="AC">Acre</li>
      <li class="aipim-combobox__option" role="option" id="state-al" data-value="AL">Alagoas</li>
      <!-- … the other 25 states -->
    </ul>
    <p class="aipim-combobox__empty" hidden>No state with that name</p>
  </div>
  <p class="aipim-field__helper" aria-live="polite" id="state-help">
    <svg class="aipim-icon aipim-field__icon" aria-hidden="true"><use href="icons/sprite.svg#aipim-error"></use></svg>
    <span>Type part of the name</span>
  </p>
</div>
```

## Do and don't

- Do: the state as a combobox, so "ba" is enough to find Bahia.
- Don't: a combobox for four options, where a person has to type to find out what the options are.

# Date picker

A Brazilian date field with a button that opens a calendar, for dates near today such as a delivery or an appointment.

## When to use

- A date the person picks by looking at the week: a delivery, an appointment, the start of a booking.
- A date with limits, where the calendar shows at once which days are allowed.

## When not to use

- A date the person knows by heart, such as the date of birth: use the date of the [Brazilian field](brazilian-field.md). Typing eight digits is faster than going back forty years month by month.
- A range of two dates (check-in and check-out): not in this version. Use two date pickers.
- A date and a time together: not in this version.

## How it works

The field is the date of the [Brazilian field](brazilian-field.md): `data-aipim-format="date"`, with the mask `dd/mm/aaaa` while you type and the check when you leave. Next to it, an [icon button](icon-button.md) opens a calendar that `aipim.js` writes under the field.

- The **calendar button** opens the calendar on the date in the field. With the field empty, it opens on today; with limits, on the nearest day allowed. Focus goes to that day.
- The **arrows** move by day (left and right) and by week (up and down), across months.
- **Home** and **End** go to the Sunday and the Saturday of the week.
- **Page Up** and **Page Down** go to the month before and after, on the same day. With **Shift**, a year.
- **Enter**, **Space** or a **click** chooses the day: the date goes in the field, the calendar closes, focus goes back to the button and the field fires `change`.
- **Escape** closes the calendar without choosing, and focus goes back to the button.
- **Tab** goes round the two month buttons and the day, inside the calendar.
- A **click outside** closes the calendar.
- After a date is chosen or typed, the button says it: "Choose date, Friday, November 20, 2026".
- A valid date inside the limits shows its day of the week on a line of its own under the helper text: "Friday, November 20". It is part of the description of the field, so a screen reader reads it with the helper text. A person who meant Friday and typed the 21st sees it without opening the calendar.

The names of the months and the week days come from `Intl`, in the language of the page (`lang`). The week starts on Sunday, as in a Brazilian calendar.

Without the script the button stays hidden and the field is a plain text field: check the value on the server too.

## Decision: typing comes first

Most date pickers make the calendar the way in and the text field an afterthought. Aipim does the opposite. The field takes the eight digits with the mask, and the calendar is a second way in, for when the day of the week matters. A person who knows the date never has to open the calendar, and a screen reader user is not forced through a grid of 30 cells to type a date they already know.

## Decision: a calendar written by the script

The calendar is not in the HTML: `aipim.js` writes it the first time the page loads, inside the field. The markup a page writes stays small (a label, an input, a button and the helper text), and the calendar is the same in every framework. The native `input type="date"` was the obvious choice, and it was the wrong one: its look and its order of day and month change with the browser and the system, it cannot take the Brazilian mask, and some browsers show no calendar at all.

## Variants and props

| Class or attribute | What it does |
|---|---|
| `aipim-field aipim-datepicker` | The wrapper. It uses the parts of the text field. |
| `aipim-field--lg` | Large field, 48px. Default is medium, 40px. The calendar stays the same size. |
| `data-aipim-format="date"` on the input | The Brazilian date: mask, check and the value as `yyyy-mm-dd` from `Aipim.br.clean`. Add `inputmode="numeric"` and `autocomplete="off"`. |
| `aipim-icon-button aipim-datepicker__button` with `aria-label` | The calendar button, 32px, inside the field. Its `aria-label` gets the date chosen after a comma. Its icon is `calendar`; the calendar takes its month icons from the same sprite. |
| `data-aipim-min`, `data-aipim-max` on the input | Optional, as `yyyy-mm-dd`. The days outside are disabled in the calendar, and a typed date outside shows an error when the person leaves. |
| `data-aipim-error-range` on the input | Your own message for a date outside the limits, in place of the default. |
| `--aipim-datepicker-day` | The size of a day in the calendar. Default `size/control-md`, 40px. |

The script adds these parts, and a page does not write them:

| Class | What it is |
|---|---|
| `aipim-datepicker__popup` | The calendar, `role="dialog"` with `aria-modal="true"`, under the field. |
| `aipim-datepicker__header` | The month buttons and the name of the month. |
| `aipim-datepicker__month` | "November 2026", `aria-live="polite"`, the name of the grid. |
| `aipim-datepicker__grid` | A `table` with `role="grid"`, one row per week. |
| `aipim-datepicker__day` | One day: a `button` inside a `td` with `role="gridcell"`, with the full date as its `aria-label`. The button takes the focus. |
| `aipim-datepicker__weekday` | The day of the week of the date in the field, a `span` at the end of the helper text, hidden while the date is empty, not valid or outside the limits. |

## States

The field has the states of the [text field](text-field.md): default, hover, focus, error and disabled. A disabled field has a disabled button. Each day in the calendar has these:

- **Default:** the number in `text/primary`.
- **Hover:** a `bg/sunken` circle.
- **Focus:** a 3px ring in `focus/ring`, inside the circle.
- **Today:** a 1px ring in `border/strong` and the number in bold.
- **Chosen:** a circle filled with `action/primary/bg`, the number in bold. Today and the chosen day are told apart by shape and weight, never by color alone.
- **Disabled** (outside the limits): the number in `text/muted`, struck through.

## Tokens used

The field, the label and the helper text use the tokens of the [text field](text-field.md). The month buttons are [icon buttons](icon-button.md). The date picker adds:

| Applies to | State | Token | Light | Dark |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Calendar button icon | All | `text/secondary` | #4A423C | #ECE5DF |
| Calendar fill | Open | `bg/surface` | #FDF9F6 | #302A25 |
| Calendar border | Open | `border/subtle` | #DAD1CA | #4A423C |
| Calendar shadow | Open | `elevation/overlay` | | |
| Month name, day | All | `text/primary` | #1A1511 | #FDF9F6 |
| Week day | All | `text/secondary` | #4A423C | #ECE5DF |
| Day fill | Hover | `bg/sunken` | #ECE5DF | #0E0A07 |
| Day ring | Today | `border/strong` | #837A73 | #A39992 |
| Day fill | Chosen | `action/primary/bg` | #B43000 | #FF9275 |
| Day number | Chosen | `action/primary/text` | #FDF9F6 | #1A1511 |
| Day number | Disabled | `text/muted` | #665D56 | #DAD1CA |
| Focus ring | Focus | `focus/ring` | #0364C2 | #AED1FE |

| Measure | Token | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Calendar button | `size/control-sm` | 32 |
| Calendar button icon | `size/icon-md` | 20 |
| Day | `size/control-md` | 40 |
| Week day row height | `size/control-sm` | 32 |
| Month buttons | `size/control-md` | 40 |
| Gap between field and calendar | `space/4` | 4 |
| Calendar padding | `space/8` | 8 |
| Calendar width | day × 7 + `space/8` × 2 + border | 298 |
| Calendar corner | `radius/md` | 8 |
| Day corner | `radius/full` | Fully round |
| Today ring | `border/thin` | 1 |
| Focus ring | `border/thick` | 3 |
| Calendar layer | `z/dropdown` | |

## Accessibility

- It follows the [ARIA date picker dialog example](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/examples/datepicker-dialog/): a button opens a modal dialog with a grid, and focus goes back to the button when it closes.
- The grid is named by the name of the month, which is a live region: moving to another month reads the new one.
- Each day has the full date as its name ("Friday, November 20, 2026"), so the month and the week day are read with it. The day is a button inside its cell, and it is the button that takes the focus, so a screen reader says the name each time. The chosen day has `aria-selected="true"` on its cell and "selected" at the end of its name, today has `aria-current="date"`, and a day outside the limits has `aria-disabled="true"`.
- No day is in the tab order (every one keeps `tabindex="-1"`) and the script moves the focus. A roving `tabindex`, which the ARIA pattern suggests, made VoiceOver in Safari say nothing on most arrow presses, because the attribute changed on the very element being focused. Tab stays inside the dialog and goes round the two month buttons and the day, and Escape always leaves it (WCAG 2.1.2).
- Escape inside a [modal](modal.md) closes the calendar first, and only the next one closes the modal.
- The week day headers are short ("Mon") with the full name in `abbr`.
- A date outside the limits shows an error with an icon and text that says the limits, never color alone.

### Screen readers

Checked by hand with each pair below. The browser checks cover the keyboard and the ARIA attributes; only a person can confirm what is read aloud.

| Screen reader | Browser | Status |
|---|---|---|
| VoiceOver (macOS) | Safari | Passed, 2026-10-30 |
| NVDA (Windows) | Firefox, Chrome | To check |
| TalkBack (Android) | Chrome | To check |

What to listen for: on the button, "Choose date" and, once there is a date, the date; on opening, "Choose date, dialog" and the day with the focus; on the arrows, each full date; on Page Down, the new month; on Enter, focus back on the button with the date chosen.

On a keyboard without the Page keys (a MacBook, most compact keyboards), Page Down is Fn and the down arrow, and Shift+Page Down is Fn, Shift and the down arrow. Both were checked. The month also changes without those keys at all: Tab reaches the two month buttons inside the calendar.

## Code examples

```html
<div class="aipim-field aipim-datepicker">
  <label class="aipim-field__label" for="delivery">Delivery date</label>
  <input class="aipim-field__control" id="delivery" type="text" inputmode="numeric" autocomplete="off" data-aipim-format="date" data-aipim-min="2026-11-02" data-aipim-max="2026-12-18" aria-describedby="delivery-help">
  <button class="aipim-icon-button aipim-datepicker__button" type="button" aria-label="Choose date">
    <svg class="aipim-icon" aria-hidden="true"><use href="icons/sprite.svg#aipim-calendar"></use></svg>
  </button>
  <p class="aipim-field__helper" aria-live="polite" id="delivery-help">
    <svg class="aipim-icon aipim-field__icon" aria-hidden="true"><use href="icons/sprite.svg#aipim-error"></use></svg>
    <span>From 02/11 to 18/12</span>
  </p>
</div>
```

## Do and don't

- Do: say the limits in the helper text, so the person knows them before opening the calendar.
- Don't: a date picker for the date of birth, where the person has to go back decades month by month.
